Original concordant: trust-be-faithful-believe-aramaic. Aramaic verb for believing or trusting - in Daniel 6:4 (no error or fault was found in him) and Daniel 6:23 (no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he believed in his God); parallel of Hebrew aman.
From √aman (firm/faithful); affirmation-formula 'it is firm'; concordantly transliterated.
Esther kept Mordecai's-command as in upbringing; Esth 2:20.

Gen-indeed-she-is-my-sister-daughter-of-my-father and Josh-in-truth-I-have-sinned (Gen 20:12; Josh 7:20). Hyphenated to distinguish the in-truth-indeed-really-aspect from H543 amen 'so-be-it' (already assigned); family with H544.

The solemn written covenant which Nehemiah and the leaders signed to keep the law - Nehemiah 9:38 (we make a sure covenant and write it); 11:23 (a fixed ordinance for the singers); from H539 aman (be-faithful-firm).
Proper noun, mountain-top north of Lebanon; Song 4:8; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Amana.
Proper noun ('faithful'); son of David; concordantly transliterated.

Affirming exclamation; 'so-it-is' (Num 22:37; Josh 7:20; 2Kgs 19:17; Ruth 3:12; Job 9:2; 12:2; 19:4,5; 34:12; 36:4; Ps 58:2). Hyphenated to distinguish the rhetorical-affirming-adverbial from H543 amen (liturgical).
Affirming-reality (Gen 18:13; Num 22:37; 1Kgs 8:27; Ps 58:2). Hyphenated to distinguish the reality-affirming-aspect from H551 amnam 'verily' (already assigned) and H61 aval 'surely'; family.
Qal: be powerful; Piel: make strong; often paired with chazaq; concordantly 'be-strong' hyphenated.

Strong-muscled or bay-spotted (of horses) - in Zechariah 6:3 (in the third chariot white horses; and in the fourth chariot strong dappled horses) and Zechariah 6:7 (the strong horses went out and sought to go); from H553 amats (be-strong).

Original concordant: Amzi-Levitical-Merarite-Ethan-father-Bani-genealogy. 1Chr-Bani-the-son-of-Shamer-the-son-of-Mahli-the-son-of-Mushi and Neh-Adaiah-the-son-of-Jeroham-the-son-of-Pelaliah-the-son-of-Amzi (1Chr 6:46; Neh 11:12 cf). Hyphenated.
Proper noun ('YHWH-is-mighty'); king of Judah; concordantly transliterated.
Root 'mr. Unambiguous speech-verb; derivatives emer (saying, H561), omer (word, H562), imrah (utterance, H565).
Aramaic; concordantly identical to H559 amar Hebrew.
From √amar (say); utterance/word; distinguished from davar (broader); concordantly 'saying'.

Utterance or poetic-saying (Job 22:28; Ps 19:3,4; 68:12; 77:9; Hab 3:9). Hyphenated to distinguish the spoken-utterance-aspect from H561 imrah 'saying' and H1697 davar 'word'; family with H559 amar 'say'.

Ezra-sacrifice-temple-dedication-hundred-bulls-two-hundred-rams-four-hundred-lambs (Ezra 6:9,17; 7:17). Hyphenated to distinguish the lamb-offering-lamb-aramaic-aspect from Hebrew H3532 keves 'lamb' (already assigned) and H561 emer 'word' (already assigned).
Priestly head of-the-sixteenth-division returned-from-exile (1Chr 9:12 = Neh 11:13, 24:14 David's-establishment-priestly-classes 'sixteenth for Immer, seventeenth for Hezir').
Proper noun, Judah-father of Uthai post-exile; 1Chr 9:4; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Imri.
Proper noun ('YHWH-has-promised'); priests and Levites in genealogies; concordantly transliterated.
Original concordant: Amraphel-king-Shinar-Mesopotamia. Gen-Amraphel-king-Shinar-Arioch-Ellasar-Chedorlaomer-Tidal-king-Goyim-coalition and Gen-same-kings-mentioned-again (Gen 14:1,9). Hyphenated.

Direct-past nightly time (Gen 19:34; 31:29,42; 2Kgs 9:26; Job 30:3). Hyphenated to distinguish the yesterday-evening-past-aspect from H8543 temol 'yesterday' and H865 etmol 'yesterday-formerly' (already assigned).

Root 'mn (be-firm, H539). Reliability, truth. The hyphenated English preserves both the relational firmness ('faithfulness') and the propositional firmness ('truth') that emet carries; English forces the choice that NL 'trouw' covers in one word. 'Truth' alone is cognitive splinter that loses the relational dimension.
Large leather-sack for grain-transport (sons of Jacob in Egypt); the hyphenated English marks function.
The Aramaic first-person-pronoun 'I' - Ezra 6:12 (I Darius have made the decree), 7:21; Daniel passim; Aramaic parallel to Hebrew ani-anokhi.

Aramaic first-person-singular pronoun 'I' (Dan 2:8,23-24 'I, Daniel, gave thanks', 3:25 'I see four men', 4:4,7,10,34-37 'I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted up my eyes', 5:16 'I have heard of you', 7:15,28, Ezra 6:12, 7:21 'I, Artaxerxes, decree'); concordantly transliterated.
Intense pleading-interjection ('oh, oh!' for prayers, Neh 1, Dan 9, Jonah); the hyphenated English marks the lament-cry.

Sighing or lamenting - in Isaiah 3:26 (her gates shall mourn and lament) and Isaiah 19:8 (the fishers also shall mourn, and all they that cast angle into the river shall lament); root of the lament-noun H592.
Death-by-accident-befallen and calamity-not-overtaking (Ex 21:13; 2Kgs 5:7; Ps 91:10). Hyphenated to distinguish the befall-meet-with-aspect from H7136b qarah-I 'happen-meet'.
Original concordant: they-masculine-plural-aramaic. The Aramaic third-person-pronoun 'they' masculine plural - Ezra 5:11, Daniel 2:44, 3:13, 6:25; Aramaic parallel to Hebrew hem.
Second-sense Aramaic innun; four-great-beasts are-four-kings; Dan 7:17.
Collective term for human in his weakness and mortality; poetic parallel for adam; concordantly 'mortal'.
Son of Seth, in whose days men began to call upon the name of YHWH (Gen 4:26; 5:6,7,9,10,11; 1Chr 1:1). 'Mortal-man'. English convention: Enosh.

Niphal: groan/sigh under oppression or grief (Ex 2:23 Israel in Egypt, Prov 29:2, Isa 24:7, Lam 1:4,8,11,21, Eze 9:4 sign on the sighing-ones, 21:6-7,11-12, Joel 1:18 animals-sigh); concordantly 'sigh'.
Feminine noun from anach (sigh, H584); inward-sound-of-suffering (Ex 2:24 'Mighty-One heard their sighing', Job 3:24, 23:2, Ps 6:7 sigh-bed-flooded, 12:6 'sighing of the needy', 31:11, 38:10).
We-servants-of-the-God-of-heaven and we-Aramaic-letter-writers-to-the-king (Ezra 4:16; 5:11; Dan 3:16). Hyphenated to distinguish the we-first-person-plural-aramaic-aspect from Hebrew H587 anachnu.
Proper noun, Issachar-city; Josh 19:19; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Anaharath.

Seafaring trading-fleet (1Kgs 9:26,27; 10:11,22; 22:49; 2Chr 8:18; 9:21; Isa 33:21; Eze 30:9). Hyphenated to mark the collective-shipping-fleet; distinguished from H591 oniyyah 'ship' (singular-vessel).
Lamentation or sighing - in Isaiah 29:2 (there shall be heaviness and sorrow) and Lamentations 2:5 (mourning and lamentation); feminine abstract from H578 anah (sigh) and pair with H8386 taaniyyah.
Proper noun, Manasseh tribe-head son of Shemida; 1Chr 7:19; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Aniam.

Plumbline-image in Amos-vision over judgment at wall (Amos 7:7 twice; 7:8 twice). Hyphenated to distinguish the plumbline-plummet-aspect from H4949 mishqeleth 'plumbline' and H6957a qav 'measuring-line'.
Personal pronoun 1cs, parallel ani (H589). Semantically equivalent; 'I' in both cases.

Num-people-became-as-complainers-evil-in-ears-of-LORD and Lam-why-does-living-man-complain-of-his-sin (Num 11:1; Lam 3:39). Hyphenated to distinguish the complain-murmur-sigh-aspect from H6049 anan-II 'practise-soothsaying'.
Qal/Hithpael: nose-snorting feel-anger (YHWH's anger against Solomon); the hyphenated English marks the emotion.
Aramaic parallel to af; face-of-Nebuchadnezzar changed; Dan 3:19.
Lev-stork-heron-after-her-kind-hoopoe-bat and Deut-stork-heron-after-her-kind-hoopoe (Lev 11:19; Deut 14:18). Hyphenated to distinguish the heron-crane-unclean-aspect from other bird-species.
Jer-the-air-filled-groaning and Eze-groaning-Jerusalem-overthrown and Eze-groaning-wounded-glittering (Jer 51:52; Eze 9:4; 24:17; 26:15). Hyphenated to distinguish the groan-cry-out-loudly-aspect.
Sighing-sound of prisoners and wounded (Ps 12:6; 79:11; 102:21; Mal 2:13). Hyphenated to distinguish the groan-moan-lament-aspect from H7581 she'agah 'roar' and H4116 mahar 'lament-cry'.
Unclean creeping-creature wall-gecko-species; Lev 11:30; concordantly transliterated.
Cling-to-an-illness to fatally-incurable (2Sam 12:15; Job 34:6; Ps 69:21; Jer 15:18; 17:9,16; 30:12,15; Mic 1:9). Hyphenated to distinguish the chronic-fatal-character from H2470 chalah 'be-sick'.
Aramaic noun: man, human; parallel to Hebrew enosh; concordantly hyphenated with language-marker.
Aramaic personal pronoun 2ms; parallel to Hebrew attah; concordantly 'you-aramaic'.
Aramaic personal pronoun 2p plural (Dan 2:8); cognate Hebrew attem.
Proper noun; king of Judah; concordantly transliterated.
Fatal-disastrous incident affecting body (Gen 42:4,38; 44:29; Ex 21:22,23). Hyphenated to distinguish the calamity-mishap-aspect from H7451 ra 'evil-misery'.
Original concordant: prison-fetter-arrest-bond-aramaic. Royal-punishment-fine-up-to-imprisonment and Daniel-bound-not-permitted and bonds-imprisonment-edict (Ezra 7:26; Dan 4:12,20). Hyphenated.

Ex-feast-of-ingathering-at-the-going-out-of-the-year and Ex-feast-of-ingathering-turn-of-the-year (Ex 23:16; 34:22). Hyphenated to distinguish the in-gathering-harvest-aspect from H625 osef 'harvest'.
From √asar (bind); held in chains (Egyptian prisoners, Joseph); concordantly 'prisoner'.

Original concordant: prisoner-collective-bound-group. Collective-prisoners as group of afflicted (Isa 10:4; 24:22; Ps 79:11; 102:21). Hyphenated to distinguish the prisoner-collective-aspect from homonym H615 asir-I 'prisoner-singular' (already assigned).
In chains-bound war-prisoner (Gen 39:20,22; Isa 10:4; 14:17; 24:22; 42:7; Ps 68:7; 69:34; 79:11; 102:21; 107:10; 146:7; Lam 3:34; Zech 9:11). Hyphenated to distinguish the fettered-captive-aspect.
Proper noun, father of Nethinim-clan returnees; Ezra 2:50; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Asnah.
Persian-king Ezra 4:10 who deported peoples; identification Asherbanipal of Assyria.
Asenath-daughter-of-Potipherah-priest-of-On and wife-of-Joseph (Gen 41:45,50; 46:20). English convention: Asenath. Egyptian 'belonging-to-Neith' or 'favourite-of-Neith' (Neith = Egyptian-goddess).
Proper noun ('he-gathered'); Levite-singer under David; concordantly transliterated.
Gatekeepers-at-the-houses-of-the-storehouse and temple-stores-gathering-places (1Chr 26:15,17; Neh 12:25). Hyphenated to distinguish the storehouse-warehouse-gathering-place-aspect from H214 otsar.
Isa-as-in-harvest-he-gathers-sheaves and Mic-harvest-time-seeking-grapes and Isa-harvest-ingathering-of-fathers (Isa 32:10; 33:4; Mic 7:1). Hyphenated.
Hapax Eccl 12:11 masters-of-collections; from H622 asaph gather.

Original concordant: diligently-precisely-aramaic. Persian loanword 'precisely/diligently' in Daniel-Ezra (Ezra 5:8; 6:8,12,13; 7:17,21,26). Hyphenated to preserve the Persian-administrative diligence; concordantly via '-aramaic'.
Proper noun, third son of Haman; Esth 9:7; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Aspatha.
Qal: bind fast, put in fetters; concordantly 'bind' across all contexts (captive, obligation, harnessing horse).
From √asar (bind, H631); self-imposed vow-binding-obligation (Num 30:2-14 complete legislation about female vows that can be annulled by father or husband); concordantly 'binding-vow'.
Aramaic 'forbidding-binding-decree' in Daniel's lions'-den-narrative (Dan 6:8,9,10,13,14,16). Hyphenated; concordantly via '-aramaic'; family with Hebrew issar.
Proper noun, son of Sennacherib successor in Assyria; Isa 37:38; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Esar-haddon.
Proper noun (possibly Persian sterre = star); queen in Esther; concordantly transliterated.
Aramaic-building-wood for temple-construction (Ezra 5:8; 6:4,11; Dan 5:4,23). Hyphenated to mark the Aramaic-parallel; distinguished from Hebrew H6086 ets 'tree-wood'.
Additive-escalative particle. Homograph with af (nose/anger, H639). Functionally 'yea-even' or 'moreover'; 'if even'.
Aramaic-additive 'also-with-existing' (Ezra 5:10,14; 6:5; Dan 6:22). Hyphenated to distinguish the also-likewise-aspect from H1571 gam 'also' (already assigned); Aramaic cognate.
Root 'np. Anatomically 'nose', idiomatically 'anger' (swollen nostrils). 'Nose' preserves the anatomical kernel that carries through both fields; 'anger' loses the anatomical basis.

Ex-you-shall-gird-him-with-the-cunningly-woven-ephod and Lev-Moses-girded-him-with-the-cunningly-woven-ephod (Ex 29:5; Lev 8:7). Hyphenated to distinguish the ephod-gird-don-aspect from H247 azar 'gird'.
Proper noun, father of Hanniel Manasseh-leader; Num 34:23; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ephod.
Qal: prepare bread on hot stone or in oven; concordantly 'bake'.
Emphatic particle in questions/reasonings: 'where then', 'what then'; the hyphenated English marks the question-emphasis.
Cultic priestly garment with breastplate; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun, ancestor of Saul; 1Sam 9:1; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Aphiah.
Spelt and rye not yet grown out; Ex 9:32.
Deep riverbed, channel through which water flows; the hyphenated English marks the object.
Dense, massive darkness; heavier than choshek (Job 3:6; 10:22; 23:17; 28:3; 30:26; Ps 11:2; 91:6; Isa 29:18; 58:10). Hyphenated to distinguish intensity-degree from H2822 choshek 'darkness'.
Deep-dark distinguished from choshek (darkness, H2822) by intensity-of-density (Ex 10:22 'three-days-darkness in Egypt felt', Deut 28:29 'groping at noon as blind in darkness').
Completely-dry-up or cease-to-exist (Gen 47:15,16; Isa 16:4; 29:20; Ps 77:9). Hyphenated to distinguish the exhausted-aspect from H3615 kalah 'complete-end'; family with H657a efes.
Substantive: utmost end, non-existent, nothingness; concordantly 'nothing'.
Proper noun ('boundary-of-bloods') battle-place David-Goliath; 1Sam 17:1; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ephes-dammim.

Original concordant: viper-poisonous-snake-desert-adder. Wicked-viper-venom-suck and Isa-viper-in-desert and Isa-snake-eggs-hatch (Job 20:16; Isa 30:6; 59:5). Hyphenated to distinguish the viper-poisonous-snake-aspect from H5175 nachash.

Water-streams or enemies threateningly surrounding (2Sam 22:5; Ps 18:5; 40:13; 116:3; Jonah 2:6). Hyphenated to distinguish the encompass-enclose-aspect from H5437 savav 'go-around' and H3803 kathar 'crown'.
Strong-inward-restraining of emotion (Gen 43:31; 45:1; Esth 5:10; Isa 42:14; 63:15; 64:11). Hyphenated to preserve the reflexive-restraint.
Several-places: Asherite-city (Josh 19:30 = Judg 1:31), Philistine-army-camp against-Israel (1Sam 4:1, 29:1), Aram-battle-place (1Kgs 20:26,30; 2Kgs 13:17). English convention: Aphek.
Proper noun, Judah-hill-country-city; Josh 15:53; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Aphekah.
Burnt-residue; sign of mourning and transience; concordantly 'ashes'.
Chicks of bird-of-prey or mother-dove (Deut 22:6; Job 39:30; Ps 84:4). Hyphenated to preserve the young-chicks-aspect.

Original concordant: Apharsachite-people-aramaic. One of the Persian people-groups colonised by Asnappar (Ashurbanipal) in Samaria, opposing the temple-rebuilding - Ezra 5:6, 6:6; presumably Persian officials or state-administrators.
Aramaic-Persian official-group (Ezra 4:9); alongside H671a Apharsachite variant of the same group.

Older-name for Bethlehem-area (Gen 35:16,19 Rachel-burial-place, 48:7 Jacob's-recollection); David's ethnic-origin (1Sam 17:12 'Ephrathite of Bethlehem', Ruth 1:2, 4:11). English convention: Ephrath / Ephratah.
Tribal-designation for Ephraimite or Bethlehemite (Judg 12:5; 1Sam 1:1; 17:12; 1Kgs 11:26; Ruth 1:2). Gentilic; family with H672 Ephrath.
Gen-sons-Gad-Haggi-Shuni-Ezbon-Eri and Num-sons-Gad-Ozni (Gen 46:16; Num 26:16). Hyphenated; Gad-fourth-son-later-variant-Ozni-Num.
Finger of human or metaphor for God's working; concordantly 'finger'.
Aramaic parallel to etsba; man's-hand-fingers writing; Dan 5:5.
Jer-in-armpits-under-arm-joints-rags and Eze-near-joints-of-hands and Eze-joints-of-arms (Jer 38:12; Eze 13:18; 41:8). Hyphenated to distinguish the joint-elbow-limb-aspect from H6504 parad.

Original concordant: set-apart-withhold-reserve-impart. Isaac's-blessing-for-Esau-not-reserved and Moses-spirit-imparted on seventy-elders (Gen 27:36; Num 11:17,25; Eze 42:6). Hyphenated to distinguish the set-apart-reserve-impart-aspect from H914 badal.
Benjamite descendant of Jonathan (1Chr 8:37,38; 9:43,44). English convention: Azel.
Pile-up valuables in storage-chambers (2Kgs 20:17; Isa 39:6; Amos 3:10; Neh 13:12,13). Hyphenated to preserve the treasure-storing-aspect; family with H214 otsar 'treasury'.
Horite tribe-head among Seir's sons (Gen 36:21,27,30; 1Chr 1:38,42). English convention: Ezer.
Proper noun, Asher-tribe-head son of Jether; 1Chr 7:38; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ara.
Areli-son-of-Gad and clan-genealogy (Gen 46:16; Num 26:17 twice). English convention: Areli. 'Lion-of-God' or 'hero-of-God'.
Qal: lie in ambush, wait to overtake; concordantly 'lie-in-wait'.
Proper noun, Judah-hill-country-city; Josh 15:52; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Arab.
The robbery-ambush of wild beasts - Job 37:8 (the wild beasts go into the den and remain in their dwellings) and 38:40 (when they lie in ambush to take prey); from H693 arav (lie-in-wait).
From √rabah (multiply); swarm-locust as plague; concordantly 'locust' (distinguished from gazam, chasil).
Window-shutter at top; at flood and at blessing/judgment-opening of heaven (Gen 7:11; 8:2; Mal 3:10; Eccl 12:3; Hos 13:3; Isa 24:18; 60:8). Hyphenated so that the cosmic function is visible.
Solomon-district 1Kgs 4:10 with Socoh and land of Hepher; place-name plural-form.
Patronym-clan David's-warrior Paarai; 2Sam 23:35; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Arbite.
Aramaic four in the Aramaic portions (Ezra 6:17; Dan 3:25; 7:2,3,6,17). Cognate of Hebrew H702. Concordantly via '-aramaic'.
Qal: cross threads on loom (priestly-clothing, blankets); concordantly 'weave'.
Bashan-region with fortified cities (Deut 3:4,13,14; 2Kgs 15:25). English convention: Argob. 'Earth-clod-region'.
Dan-aramaic-clothed-with-purple and Dan-aramaic-clothed-with-purple-Daniel and Dan-aramaic-promise-of-purple-garment (Dan 5:7,16,29). Hyphenated.

Original concordant: chest-travel-chest-baggage-chest-loading-chest. Ark-cows-cart-argaz-beside-ark and Philistines-trespass-offering-in-chest (1Sam 6:8,11,15). Hyphenated to distinguish the chest-travel-chest-baggage-chest-aspect from H727 aron 'ark-chest' (already assigned).
Expensive red-purple dye from sea-snail; colour of nobility and sanctuary; concordantly 'purple'.
Original concordant: Ard-son-Benjamin-tribe-head. Gen-sons-Benjamin-Bela-Becher-Ashbel-Gera-Naaman-Ehi-Rosh-Muppim-Huppim-Ard and Num-sons-Benjamin-Ard (Gen 46:21; Num 26:40). Hyphenated.
Proper noun, son of Caleb; 1Chr 2:18; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ardon.
Patronym-clan son of Benjamin; Num 26:40; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ardite.
Pluck or pick fruits-vine-leaves - in Psalm 80:13 (all who pass by the way pluck him) and Song of Songs 5:1 (I gather my myrrh with my spice); concrete action of breaking off.
Aramaic-deictic interjection in visions (Dan 7:2,5,6,7,8,13). Hyphenated to mark the Aramaic-parallel; distinguished from Hebrew H7200 ra'ah 'see'.

Original concordant: proper-name-Arvad-Phoenician-island-city. Proper noun Arvad (Phoenician island-city, modern Ruad) - in Ezekiel 27:8 (the inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad were your rowers) and Ezekiel 27:11 (the men of Arvad with your army were on your walls round about).
Proper noun, son of Gad; Num 26:17; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Arod.
Original concordant: Arodi-son-Gad-Arodites-clan. Gen-and-the-sons-of-Gad-Ziphion-and-Haggi-Arodi-and-Areli and Num-of-Arod-the-family-of-the-Arodites (Gen 46:16; Num 26:17). Hyphenated.

Original concordant: stalls-horse-mangers-Solomon-royal-stud. 1K-Solomon-had-forty-thousand-horse-stalls-for-his-chariots and 2Chr-Solomon-had-four-thousand-horse-stalls-and-chariots (1K 4:26 par; 2Chr 9:25; cf 32:28). Hyphenated.
Healing-of wound or people-destruction (2Chr 24:13; Neh 4:1; Jer 8:22; 30:17; 33:6; Isa 58:8). Hyphenated to distinguish the healing-restoration-aspect from H4832 marpe 'healing' and H7499 refuah.
Proper noun, place where Abimelech stayed; Judg 9:41; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Arumah.
Unique lexeme. Wooden chest (covenant-ark, coffin, money-chest). 'Ark' covers all contexts; 'chest' is competing but 'ark' is the standard convention for this specific lexeme.
Jebusite-owner of-threshing-floor-on-Moriah where David-altar-built after-plague-halt (2Sam 24:16,18,20-24 core-account). English convention: Araunah.
Cedar-tree (cedrus libani); concordantly 'cedar'; same tree-species across all contexts.
Old-man-wayfarer-Gibeah and Job-wayfarer-with-the-wicked and traveller-disciplining (Judg 19:17; Job 34:8; Ps 139:3). Hyphenated to distinguish the travel-journey-wayfarer-aspect from H1980 halakh.
Asherite family-head and post-exile-family-ancestor (1Chr 7:39; Ezra 2:5; Neh 6:18; 7:10). English convention: Arah. 'Wayfarer-traveller'.
Beaten path, often poetic; distinguished from derech (way) and mesillah (highway); concordantly 'path'.
Aramaic word for path or conduct - in Daniel 4:37 (all His ways are right) and Daniel 5:23 (the God in whose hand your breath is and to whom all your paths belong); parallel of Hebrew orach.
Gen-caravan-Ishmaelites-came-from-Gilead-camels-laden and Isa-behold-caravan-Dedanites (Gen 37:25; Isa 21:13). Hyphenated to distinguish the caravan-travellers-aspect from H734 orach 'path'.
Fixed-allotted food-ration for prisoner or guest (2Kgs 25:30; Jer 40:5; 52:34; Prov 15:17). Hyphenated to preserve the fixed-food-portion.
Variant-spelling of aryeh; concordantly 'lion-II' (same species, parallel in poetic texts).
Adult lion as predator and image of strength; concordantly 'lion' (distinguished from kefir young-lion).
Mighty-man of David, prophetic-name of Jerusalem (2Sam 23:20; 1Chr 11:22; Ezra 8:16; Isa 29:1,2,7). 'Lion-of-God'. English convention: Ariel.

Original concordant: altar-hearth-fire-hearth-of-God. Altar-hearth or fire-hearth of God (literally 'lion-of-God') - in Ezekiel 43:15 (the altar-hearth shall be four cubits) and Ezekiel 43:16 (the altar-hearth shall be twelve cubits in length); burnt-offering.
Proper noun, ninth son of Haman; Esth 9:9; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Aridai.
Proper noun, sixth son of Haman; Esth 9:8; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Aridatha.
Aramaic cognate of ari (lion, H738b); exclusive in Dan 6:8,13,17,20-21,25,28, 7:4 'first-beast like-lion, eagle's-wings had-it' - symbolic-empire-image.
Proper noun, fellow-killer with Pekah against Pekahiah; 2Kgs 15:25; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Arieh.
Gen-Arioch-king-Ellasar-in-coalition-with-Amraphel and Gen-same-kings-repetition and Dan-Arioch-head-of-king's-bodyguard (Gen 14:1,9; Dan 2:14,15,24,25). Hyphenated.
Aramaic form Babylonian-king's-guard-captain (Dan 2:14-25); alongside H746a Arioch-Elam-king Gen 14.
Proper noun, eighth son of Haman; Esth 9:9; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Arisai.
Qal/Hiphil: extend in time or space, prolong; the hyphenated English marks state.
From √arach (be-long); long-of-nose (delaying anger), attribute of YHWH 'long-suffering and merciful'; the hyphenated English marks the patient-restrained-anger.
Proper noun, city in Shinar; Gen 10:10; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Erech.
Jer-exile-prolonged and Job-prolonged-complaint and 2S-prolonged-strife-between-Saul's-house-and-David (Jer 29:28; Job 11:9; 2S 3:1). Hyphenated.

Original concordant: prolongation-life-span-extension-aramaic. Aramaic word for prolongation or extension of time - in Daniel 4:27 (that there may be a prolongation of your tranquillity) and Daniel 7:12 (a prolongation of life was given to them); temporal-extension.
Aramaic for knees of Belshazzar striking-each-other; Dan 5:6.
Family-designation in Ephraim-border (Josh 16:2; 2Sam 15:32; 16:16; 17:5,14; 1Chr 27:33). Gentilic for Archite-tribe from which came Hushai the friend of David.
Proper noun (people and land). English convention Aram.
Fortified residence, citadel within the city; concordantly 'citadel'.
Ethnonym for inhabitant of Aram-Naharaim/Aram-Damascus (Gen 25:20 Bethuel-Aramean, 28:5 Laban, 31:20,24 Laban-Aramean-vs-Jacob), national-confession (Deut 26:5 'A wandering Aramean was my father').
Original concordant: aramaic-Aramaic-language-in-aramaic. Rabshakeh-speak-in-Aramaic-not-in-Judaic and Daniel-Aramaic-answer and Ezra-letter-in-Aramaic (2Kgs 18:26; Dan 2:4; Ezra 4:7). Hyphenated.
Mesopotamian Syria between-two-rivers (Gen 24:10; Deut 23:5; Judg 3:8; Ps 60:2). Compound 'Aram-of-the-two-rivers'; family with H758 Aram.
Proper noun, son of Saul + Rizpah delivered to Gibeonites; 2Sam 21:8; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Armoni.
Original concordant: Aran-son-Dishan-Horite-Seir. Gen-sons-Dishan-Uz-Aran and 1Chr-sons-Dishan-Uz-Aran (Gen 36:28; 1Chr 1:42). Hyphenated.
Hapax Isa 44:14 wood-species-alongside cypress and oak; identity-tree possibly laurel.
Proper noun, son of Jerahmeel; 1Chr 2:25; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Oren.
Proper noun; border-river between Moab and Ammon; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun, descendant of David post-exile; 1Chr 3:21; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Arnan.
Jebusite-thresher whose threshing-floor David bought as temple-site (1Chr 21:15-28, 2Chr 3:1); parallel to Araunah in 2Sam 24; concordantly transliterated.
Aramaic noun: land, earth, ground; parallel to Hebrew erets; concordantly hyphenated with language-marker.
Aramaic for bottom-of-lions'-den for men; Dan 6:24.
Aramean city north of Hamath (2Kgs 18:34; 19:13; Isa 10:9; 36:19; 37:13; Jer 49:23). English convention: Arpad.
Son of Shem, third-in-line of Shem and ancestor-of-Abraham (Gen 10:22,24 = 1Chr 1:17-18,24, 11:10-13 Semitic-genealogy).
Unique lexeme. Covers semantically from local area to earth-floor. Concordantly holds one English word for one Hebrew lexeme.
Proper noun, palace-administrator of king Elah; 1Kgs 16:9; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Arza.
Aramaic parallel to erets; idols-without-earth-making; Jer 10:11.
Qal: curse (call down evil); distinguished from qalal (consider light/curse); concordantly 'curse'.
Ararat-mountains where ark-lands and judgment-call (Gen 8:4; 2Kgs 19:37; Isa 37:38; Jer 51:27). English convention: Ararat. Toponym-mountain-range-Armenia in North-Mesopotamia.
Piel: betroth as legally-binding pre-marriage-promise (Ex 22:16, Deut 20:7, 22:23-28, 28:30, 2Sam 3:14 David-Michal). Concordantly 'betroth'.
Persian sovereign Artaxerxes in Ezra and Nehemiah (Ezra 4:7,8,11,23; 7:1,7,11,12,21; 8:1; Neh 2:1; 5:14; 13:6). English convention: Artaxerxes.
Original concordant: Artaxerxes-aramaic-variant. Persian-king Artaxerxes in alternative-spelling. English convention: Artaxerxes-variant. Distinguished from H783a.
Aramaic parallel to esh; body-fourth-beast in fire; Dan 7:11.
The foundations of the rebuilt temple - Ezra 4:12, 5:16, 6:3; Aramaic, possibly Persian loanword, related to walls-foundation H846 ushrana.
Ashbel-son-of-Benjamin and clan-genealogy (Gen 46:21; Num 26:38; 1Chr 8:1). English convention: Ashbel. 'Man-of-Baal' or 'fire-of-Baal'.
Patronym-clan son of Benjamin; Num 26:38; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ashbelite.
Proper noun, son of Dishan; Gen 36:26; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Eshban.
Proper noun, linen-worker-clan Shelah-Judah-branch; 1Chr 4:21; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ashbea.
Mountain-slopes on the east side of the Dead Sea (Deut 3:17; 4:49; Josh 10:40; 12:3,8; 13:20). 'Slopes'. English convention: Ashdoth.
Proper noun; city of the Philistine pentapolis, centre of the Dagon-cult; concordantly transliterated.
Inhabitant of the Philistine city Ashdod (Josh 13:3; 1Sam 5:6,7; Neh 4:1; 13:23,24). Gentilic; family with H795 Ashdod.
Fiery-law from the right hand of YHWH; Deut 33:2.
From √esh (fire); offering consumed by fire; the hyphenated English preserves the burnt-cultic dimension.
Root 'nsh; female counterpart ish (H376). Also 'wife'; context decides.
Foundation or supporting stone-work - in Isaiah 16:7 (you shall mourn for the foundations of Kir-Hareseth) and parallel-text; architecture-base of Moabite city-bulwark in oracle.
Proper noun (people and land). English convention Asshur; 'Assyria' is a later geographical choice.
Proper noun people, descendant of Dedan; Gen 25:3; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Asshurim.
Hapax 2Sam 2:9 preposition-variant; orthographic form alongside the standard H413 el.
Proper noun, Hamath-deity; 2Kgs 17:30; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ashima.
Raisin-cake as love-comfort or feast-gift (2Sam 6:19; 1Chr 16:3; Hos 3:1; Song 2:5). Hyphenated to distinguish the raisin-cake-aspect from H6778 tsimmuq 'raisin-cake' and H5692 ugah.
Cluster of grapes; explicit in the spies-episode and the parables of Isaiah (Gen 40:10; Num 13:23,24; Deut 32:32; Song 1:14; 7:7,8,9; Isa 65:8; Mic 7:1). Hyphenated.
Ally of Abraham and the name-giving valley near Hebron (Gen 14:13,24; Num 13:23,24; 32:9; Deut 1:24). English convention: Eshcol. Family with H811 eshkol 'cluster-of-grapes'.
Ashkenaz-people-son of Gomer and war-call against Babel (Gen 10:3; 1Chr 1:6; Jer 51:27). English convention: Ashkenaz. 'Scytho-Cimmerian-people'.
The gift-tribute that peoples bring to Zion or the trading-partner - Psalm 72:10 (the kings of Tarshish and the isles shall offer presents) and Ezekiel 27:15 (they brought you in payment).
Abraham's-tamarisk in Beersheba and Saul-resting-place (Gen 21:33; 1Sam 22:6; 31:13). Distinguished from H427 alah 'oak' and H424 elah 'terebinth' (already assigned) and H436 elon.
Qal: take guilt upon oneself; Niphal: be found guilty; the hyphenated English marks state.
From √asham (be-guilty); offering for restitution upon transgression; distinguished from chattath (sin-offering); concordantly 'guilt-offering'.
Joseph-brothers-confess-guilt and human-becoming-guilty (Gen 42:21; 2Sam 14:13; Hos 14:1). Hyphenated to distinguish the guilty-punishable-aspect from H7561a rasha 'wicked' (already assigned).
From √asham (be-guilty); state of guilt and the awareness of it; the hyphenated English marks the inward burden.
Third part of the night as watch-period (Ex 14:24; Judg 7:19; 1Sam 11:11; Ps 63:7; 90:4; Lam 2:19). Hyphenated to preserve the night-watch-interval; family with H8104 shamar 'guard'.
Original concordant: Ashnah-city-Judah-Shephelah-lowland. Josh-Eshtaol-Zorah-Ashnah and Josh-Iphtah-Ashnah-Nezib (Josh 15:33,43). Hyphenated.
Proper noun, Judah-hill-country-city; Josh 15:52; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Eshan.
Diviner or magician - in Daniel 1:20 (above all the magicians and astrologers in his whole kingdom) and Daniel 2:2 (the king commanded to call the magicians and astrologers); court-class.
Professional-magician at Babylonian court (Dan 1:20; 2:2,10,27; 4:4; 5:7,11,15). Hyphenated to distinguish the enchant-magic-aspect from H2748 chartom 'magician' and H3784 kashaf 'practise-sorcery'.
Carrying-case for arrows of archer (Job 39:23; Ps 127:5; Isa 22:6; 49:2; Jer 5:16; Lam 3:13). Hyphenated to preserve the arrows-case-aspect.
Proper noun, Babylonian eunuch-commander Daniel-context; Dan 1:3; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ashpenaz.
Refuse-rubble-mound outside the city-gate (1Sam 2:8; Neh 2:13; 3:13,14; Ps 113:7; Lam 4:5). Hyphenated to preserve the rubble-rubbish-aspect.
Philistine coastal-city (Judg 1:18, 1Sam 6:17, 2Sam 1:20, Jer 25:20, 47:5-7, Amos 1:8, Zeph 2:4-7, Zech 9:5); concordantly transliterated.
Inhabitant of Ashkelon-Philistine; Josh 13:3; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ashkelonite.
Piel: declare to be blessed; the hyphenated English marks the action (distinguished from ashar II 'set-paces').
Root 'shr (go-straight, connect). Pan-functional relative. English 'which' covers the relative function broadly; 'that', 'who' are grammatical variants of the same relative.
Conjunction-use of asher: 'that, where, because'; the hyphenated English distinguishes from rel.pron.
Preposition-use of asher (mostly 'me-asher' = 'from-what'); the hyphenated English distinguishes from rel.pron and conjunction.
Compound ke+asher. Comparative/temporal conjunction. 'As' covers both functions.
Exclamation-noun 'blessed is...'; distinguished from barak (bless) and berakhah (blessing); concordantly 'blessed-II'.
Proper noun; son and tribe of Israel; concordantly transliterated.
Footsteps on the way, figuratively conduct of life (Job 31:7; Ps 17:5; 37:31; 44:19; 73:2; Prov 14:15; Isa 58:13). Hyphenated to mark footprint; distinguished from H6541 par'os 'single-step'.

The people or tribe over which Ish-bosheth was made king - 2Samuel 2:9 (over Gilead, over the Ashurites, over Jezreel); possibly Asher-tribe-variant; Ezekiel 27:6 (your decks they have made of cypress).
Proper noun, Cyprian-cypress-species ship-deck; Eze 27:6; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bath-ashurim.
Proper noun, son of Jehallelel-Judah-branch; 1Chr 4:16; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Asarel.
Proper noun, Levi-singer son of Asaph; 1Chr 25:2; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Asarelah.
Canaanite fertility-goddess, also her cult-pole; concordantly transliterated (no English equivalent).
Patronym-clan tribe Asher; Judg 1:32; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Asherite.
Asriel-son-of-Gilead and Manassite tribe-head (Num 26:31; Josh 17:2; 1Chr 7:14). English convention: Asriel. 'I-am-rejoiced-by-God' or 'God-is-prosperity'.
Patronym-clan son of Manasseh; Num 26:31; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Asrielite.
The foundation-walls of the rebuilt temple about which Tattenai reported to Darius - Ezra 5:3, 5:9; Aramaic Persian loanword, possibly panel-work or wooden frame.
City on the border of Judah and Dan, Samson's camp (Josh 15:33; 19:41; Judg 13:25; 16:31; 18:2,8,11; 1Chr 2:53). English convention: Eshtaol.
Patronym-clan from Eshtaol; 1Chr 2:53; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Eshtaolite.
Aramaic rebellion-uprising (Ezra 4:15,19 Jerusalem-accusation); word-stem uncertain, possibly Persian-loan.
Priestly-city in Judah's hill-country (Josh 15:50; 21:14; 1Sam 30:28; 1Chr 4:17,19; 6:57). English convention: Eshtemoa.

Dan-aramaic-signs-of-the-Most-High and Dan-aramaic-great-signs-and-wonders and Dan-aramaic-signs-Nebuchadnezzar (Dan 3:32,33; 6:28). Hyphenated to distinguish the sign-wonder-aramaic-aspect from H226 ot.

Nota accusativi. Marks the determinate direct object; no lexical content, purely syntactic. Concordantly rendered as the untranslated sign « to keep the particle visible without adding English semantics.

Preposition of accompaniment, homograph with the nota accusativi (H853) but functionally distinct. 'With' is the standard equivalent; semantically overlaps with im (H5973a) but etymologically distinct.

Iron implement for plough or digging (1Sam 13:20,21; Isa 2:4; Jer 26:15; Mic 4:3; Joel 4:10). Hyphenated to preserve the plowshare-mattock-aspect; distinguished from homonym H853 eth-I (accusative-marker).
Proper noun, Sidonian king father of Jezebel; 1Kgs 16:31; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ethbaal.
Aramaic/poetic Hebrew: approach, come; parallel to bo; concordantly 'come-aramaic'.
Aramaic verb: approach, arrive; parallel to Hebrew bo; concordantly compound with language-marker.
Personal pronoun 2ms. 'You' is kernel-form (English does not distinguish singular/plural in modern usage; thou/thee are archaic).
Pers.pron. 2sg. feminine: you (addressing Ruth, bride in Song); the hyphenated English marks gender.
Second-person singular feminine; concordantly 'you-woman' to mark gender explicitly (H859a = masculine, H859b = generic).
Personal pronoun 2mp. Counterpart of atah (H859a). 'You-plural' standard.
Second-person feminine-plural personal-pronoun (Gen 31:6; Eze 13:11,20; 34:17,31). Hyphenated to distinguish the feminine-plural-pronoun-aspect from H859d 'you-plural' (masc.).
Female riding-animal, calm and valuable; concordantly 'she-donkey' (distinguished from chamor donkey).
Aramaic-specific term for fire-heated-furnace - exclusively in Daniel 3:6,11,15,17,19-23,26 'fiery-furnace-burning of-fire' - actually built-furnace into which Shadrach-Meshach-Abednego-were-cast.
Philistine-mercenary who remained loyal to David (2Sam 15:19,21,22; 18:2,5,12; 23:29). 'Near-me'. English convention: Ittai.
Wilderness-edge-place on exodus-route (Ex 13:20; Num 33:6,7,8). English convention: Etham. 'Boundary-post'.

Time-marker 'from-yesterday' / 'formerly' (1Sam 4:7; 14:21; 19:7; 21:6; 2Sam 3:17; 5:2; 2Kgs 13:5; Isa 30:33; Mic 2:8). Hyphenated; distinguished phraseologically-adverbially from H8543 temol 'yesterday'.
Proper noun, Gershon-Levi-genealogy; 1Chr 6:41; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ethni.
Specific payment-wage to temple-or-street-prostitutes distinguished from sakhar (work-wage, H7939) (Deut 23:19, Isa 23:17,18, Eze 16:31,34,41, Hos 9:1, Mic 1:7).
Proper noun, son of Helah-Ashur-Tekoa-Judah-branch; 1Chr 4:7; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ethnan.
Aramaic-cognate for location or spot (Ezra 5:15; 6:3,5,7; Dan 2:35). Hyphenated to preserve the Aramaic-parallel of H4725 maqom 'place' (Hebrew).
Proper noun, caravan-road in Negev; Num 21:1; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Atharim.
Original concordant: wall-foundation-aramaic-ashrna. Aramaic-Persian-loan walls-and-foundations (Ezra 4:12, 5:3, 5:9); identity Persian uncertain.
Beer-travel-stop-of-Israel in wilderness and Beer-city-Jotham (Num 21:16,18; Judg 9:21). English convention: Beer-place. Family with H875 beer 'well-spring' (already assigned).
Dug well with water; distinguished from ayin (natural spring); concordantly 'well'.
Water-cistern at Bethlehem-gate from which David's mighty men drew (2Sam 23:15,16; 1Chr 11:17,18). Hyphenated to distinguish the cistern-water-aspect from homonyms H953a bor-I 'pit' and H1252 bor-II.
Proper noun, Asher tribe-head son of Zophah; 1Chr 7:37; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beera.
Proper noun ('well-of-the-mighty') Moab-border; Isa 15:8; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beer-elim.
Proper noun, Reuben tribe-head carried away by Tilgath-Pilneser; 1Chr 5:6; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beerah.
Gibeonite city in Benjaminite territory (Josh 9:17; 18:25; 2Sam 4:2; Ezra 2:25; Neh 7:29). English convention: Beeroth. 'Wells'.
Proper noun, Hittite father of Judith; Gen 26:34; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beeri.
Well of the Living-One-who-sees-me where Hagar and Isaac dwelt (Gen 16:14; 24:62; 25:11). English convention: Beer-Lahai-Roi. Composition 'well-of-the-living-seeing-me', sacred-place-Negev.
Proper noun ('well-of-seven/oath'); city in southern Canaan; concordantly transliterated.
One of the stops of Israel during the wilderness-journey, at the wells of the Jaakan-sons - Deuteronomy 10:6; in Numbers 33:31-32 as Bene-Jaakan.
Designation of inhabitants of Beeroth (2Sam 4:2,5,9; 23:37). Gentilic; family with H881 Be'eroth.
Qal: emit foul odour, become morally repulsive; concordantly 'stink' (also metaphorically 'be-hated').
Aramaic Peal; king-displeased about Daniel-plot; Dan 6:14.
Original concordant: stench-foul-odour-pus-corruption-decay. Isa-instead-of-balsam-stench and Joel-stench-of-army-camps and Amos-stench-of-army-camps (Isa 3:24; Joel 2:20; Amos 4:10). Hyphenated.
Hapax Job 31:40 stinkweed-instead-of-wheat; from H889 boshet stench.
Stinking wild grapes - in Isaiah 5:2 (He looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes) and Isaiah 5:4 (why brought it forth wild grapes?).
Priestly family-head after the exile (Ezra 2:11; 8:11; 10:28; Neh 7:16; 10:16). English convention: Bebai.
Proper noun. English convention Babel (not Babylon, which is Greek).
Aramaic proper noun; empire and capital; transliteration, language-marker links to Hebrew Babel.
Aramaic gentilic Babylonians (Ezra 4:9); from H894 Bavel.
Qal: break covenant/trust; the hyphenated English compounds 'deal-treacherously'.

Original concordant: treachery-betrayal-faithlessness. Treachery or betrayal - in Isaiah 24:16 (the treacherous deal treacherously, yea, the treacherous deal very treacherously) and Jeremiah 12:1 (why are all who deal treacherously secure?); homograph of beged.
Unique lexeme. Item of clothing. 'Garment' covers both mantle and general robe; 'clothing' is too generic.
Treacherous or betraying - in Jeremiah 3:7 (and her treacherous sister Judah saw it) and Jeremiah 3:10 (only feignedly, not faithfully); participial adjective of H898 bagad.
Post-exilic family-head returned from Babel (Ezra 2:2,14; 8:14; Neh 7:7,19; 10:17). English convention: Bigvai.
Proper noun, third eunuch attendant of Ahasuerus; Esth 1:10; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bigtha.
One of the two threshold-keeper-eunuchs who plotted against Ahasuerus and were hanged through Mordecai's report - Esther 2:21, 6:2; his fellow-conspirator was Teresh.
Root bdd (be-alone). Mostly with preposition le-vaddo ('to-his-separation' = 'alone'). 'Separation' preserves the nominal form; 'alone' is functional translation of the preposition-complex.
Fine fabric for priestly clothing; distinguished from bad I 'pole/carrying-beam' and III 'alone'; concordantly 'linen'.
Vain-speech or lying inventions (Job 11:3; Isa 16:6; 44:25; Jer 48:30; 50:36). Hyphenated to distinguish the empty-invention-aspect from H3577 kazav 'lie' and H8267 sheqer 'deceit'.
Solitary-dwell of leper or people (Lev 13:46; Num 23:9; Jer 15:17; Hos 8:9; Ps 102:8). Hyphenated to distinguish the separation-loneliness-aspect from H905 bad 'alone' and H910 badad-adv 'lonely'.
From √badal (separate, H914); state-of-alone-apart-separated (Lev 13:46 leper 'separated shall-he-dwell', Num 23:9 Balaam-on-Israel 'people that dwells apart and is-not-counted-among-nations').
Proper noun, son of Bani who took foreign-wife; Ezra 10:35; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bedeiah.
Base metal which is separated-out (Num 31:22; Isa 1:25; Eze 22:18,20; 27:12; Zech 4:10). Hyphenated to preserve the tin-by-metal-aspect.
Hiphil: set apart, divide (cultic: holy from common); Niphal: separate oneself; concordantly 'separate'.
Hapax-form; shepherd-rescues two-feet-pieces from lion's-mouth; Amos 3:12.
Original concordant: bdellium-precious-resin-fragrant-gum. Gen-bdellium-land-of-Havilah-gold-and-bdellium-and-onyx-stone and Num-manna-as-bdellium-appearance (Gen 2:12; Num 11:7). Hyphenated.
Crack-in-wall-or-building requiring-repair (2Kgs 12:6,7,8,9,13 Joash-temple-restoration 'repair of-house-of-YHWH', 22:5 = 2Chr 34:10 Josiah's-reforms 'bedeq of-house', 2Chr 34:5).
Proper noun, Jehu's-captain; 2Kgs 9:25; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bidkar.

Waste-and-void primaeval-state and judgment-reversal (Gen 1:2; Isa 34:11; Jer 4:23). Hyphenated to distinguish the void-emptiness-chaos-aspect from H8414 tohu 'desolation' (already assigned) and H772 erets.
White-coloured marble in palace of Vashti-feast; Esth 1:6.
Aramaic hurriedness (Ezra 4:23 with-haste to Jerusalem); from √bhl hasten.
Niphal: suddenly fall into panic; Piel: hurry/hasten; the hyphenated English marks state.
Aramaic cognate of behal (be-terrified, H926); Peal/Pael/Ithpaal: suddenly-startle-or-hurry (Dan 2:25, 3:24, 4:5,19, 5:6,9,10, 7:15,28).
Fright-bewilderment by sickness or judgment (Lev 26:16; Ps 78:33; Isa 65:23; Jer 15:8). Hyphenated to distinguish the dismay-panic-aspect from H2844 chath 'terror' and H368 eymah 'fear'.
Unique lexeme. Four-legged (domestic) animal, collective. 'Beast' covers the generic animal-collectivity; 'cattle' is too narrowly economic.
From √bhr (shine brightly); white/bright skin-patch in diagnostic-procedure Lev 13-14; the hyphenated English marks light-glance + local-phenomenon.
Root bw'. Movement inward or toward. Derivative mavo (entrance, H3996).

Qal: hold for nothing, dismiss with contempt; distinguished from bazah (despise, H959) - buz is the dismissive-contempt-mode (Gen 38:23, Prov 1:7, 6:30, 11:12, 13:13, 14:21, 23:9,22, Neh 2:19, Zech 4:10).
Nominal counterpart of bazah (despise, H959); state-or-object of being-held-in-contempt (Gen 38:23 Judah 'let us be contempt', Job 12:5,21, 31:34, Ps 31:19, 119:22, 123:3,4).
Buz-son-of-Nahor and Israel's-judgment-people (Gen 22:21; Job 32:2,6; Jer 25:23). English convention: Buz. Distinguished from homonym H937 buz-'contempt' (already assigned); Arab-desert-tribe.
The Aramean tribe from which Elihu's family originated - Job 32:2, 32:6; presumably descended from Buz, son of Nahor (Gen 22:21).
Proper noun, priest-father of Ezekiel; Eze 1:3; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Buzi.
Proper noun, Levitical wall-rebuilder; Neh 3:18; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bavvai.

Confused-Israelites-in-wilderness and Egyptians-bewildered (Ex 14:3; Joel 1:18; Esth 3:15). Hyphenated to distinguish the confused-trapped-wandering-aspect from H7686 shagah 'wander' (already assigned).

The food-fruit which the mountains bring forth for Behemoth - Job 40:20 (the mountains bring him forth food, where all the beasts of the field play) and Isaiah 44:19 (have I not made the half thereof bread).
Proper noun, eighth month (October/November); 1Kgs 6:38; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bul.
Proper noun, son of Jerahmeel; 1Chr 2:25; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bunah.
Qal/Hithpolel: tread underfoot (Ps 44:6, 60:14, 108:14 'Mighty-One shall trample', 119:118, Prov 27:7, Isa 14:19,25, 63:6,18, Jer 12:10, Eze 16:6, Zech 10:5); concordantly 'trample'.
Late-OT Persian loanword for fine linen (1Chr 4:21; 15:27; 2Chr 2:13; 3:14; 5:12; Esth 1:6; 8:15; Eze 27:16). Hyphenated; distinguished from H8336b shesh-II 'byssus' (Egyptian-variant).
Proper noun, sharp rock-point on Philistine-pass; 1Sam 14:4; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bozez.
Hapax Eccl 9:1 heart-set-forth-investigate; root √bur-II (not H953 pit).
Hewn-out water-pit or cistern; also used as prison; distinguished from beer (well-spring); concordantly 'pit'.
Second-sense bor; cistern Sirah where Abner went; 2Sam 3:26.
Root bwsh. 'Be-ashamed' preserves the stative shame-state.
Shame-cover at enemy-triumph and sin-result (Ps 89:46; Mic 7:10; Obad 10; Eze 7:18). Hyphenated to distinguish the shame-disgrace-aspect from H2781 cherpah 'reproach-shame' (already assigned).
Cleave or cut through as river through land - in Isaiah 18:2 and Isaiah 18:7 (both occurrences in the expression: a people whose land the rivers divide) - rare verb for geographical division.
Qal: scorn, esteem-low, hold for worthless; concordantly 'despise'.

Abstract-nominal form of bazaz (take-plunder, H962) parallel-with shalal (booty, H7998) but marks acquired-spoils-as-goods-in-possession (2Chr 14:13 Asa 'great spoils-good in-hand', 25:13 substitutes-for).
Qal: rob, plunder, spoil; the hyphenated English marks action plus object.
Proper noun, Judah-city south; Josh 15:28; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Biziothiah.
Bezek-city where Judah-Adoni-bezek-defeats and Saul's-monster-numbering (Judg 1:4,5; 1Sam 11:8). English convention: Bezek. 'Splinter' or 'lightning-bolt' (possibly-family-with bazaq-flash).
Scatter and lavishly distribute - in Psalm 68:31 (He scatters peoples that delight in war) and Daniel 11:24 (he shall scatter among them prey, spoil, and goods); intensive action of distributing.
Proper noun, second eunuch attendant of Ahasuerus; Esth 1:10; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bizzetha.
Passive participle of bachar (choose): the chosen one, man in the prime of his life; concordantly 'young-man'.

Watchtower or siege-tower - in Isaiah 23:13 (they set up the towers of Assyria against her) and Isaiah 32:14 (the palace shall be forsaken; the multitude of the city shall be left; Ophel and the watchtower).

From √bachar (choose, H977); passive-participle 'one-chosen': Saul's family (2Sam 21:6), Jacob-Israel-status (Ps 105:6,43 = 1Chr 16:13, 106:5, Isa 43:20, 45:4, 65:9,15,22), YHWH-Servant par excellence.
Qal: investigate-prove, verify (people by YHWH); concordantly 'test'.
Patronym-clan David's-warrior Azmaveth; 1Chr 11:33; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Baharumite.
Benjamite place on road to Jordan (2Sam 3:16; 16:5; 17:18; 19:17; 1Kgs 2:8). English convention: Bahurim. 'Young-men-place'.

Hasty or unconsidered speech without deliberation - in Psalm 106:33 (they provoked his spirit so that he spoke unadvisedly with his lips) and Proverbs 12:18 (there is one who speaks like the piercings of a sword).
From √batach (trust); state of certainty and rest; adverbial 'safely'; concordantly 'safety'.
Proper noun, Aramean place where David seized bronze; 2Sam 8:8; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Betah.

Original concordant: confidence-assurance-grounds-trust-life. 2K-thus-says-the-great-king-the-king-of-Assyria-what-confidence-is-this-wherein-you-trust and Eccl-for-a-living-dog-is-better-than-a-dead-lion (2K 18:19; Eccl 9:4 cf). Hyphenated.
Hapax Eccl 12:3 grinders-ceased-labour; Aramaic-loan also in later Hebrew.
Aramaic-verb for ceasing or halting building-work (Ezra 4:21,23,24; 5:5; 6:8). Hyphenated to mark the Aramaic-parallel; distinguished from Hebrew batel 'cease'.
Anatomical body-part, including womb; concordantly 'belly' (not 'womb' - that is contextual interpretation).
Preposition: 'for', 'through', in protection of; the hyphenated English marks the relation.
Gift from the best of the land; Gen 43:11.
Proper noun, Gad-place; Josh 13:26; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Betonim.
Pleading-interjection: 'with-your-permission, lord' (Judah to Joseph, Moses to YHWH); the hyphenated English marks the polite-address.
Root byn. Discern, understand. 'Discern' preserves the cognitive distinction-action; derived bein (H996), tevunah (H8394).
Root byn (discern, H995). 'Between' holds the distinction-spatial aspect.
From √bin; ability to see-through, between-see, clarity-of-understanding; distinguished from tevunah and chokmah; concordantly 'discernment'.
Aramaic parallel to binah; God gives-understanding; Dan 2:21.
Laid eggs of birds or quails (Deut 22:6; Job 6:6; 39:14; Isa 10:14; 59:5). Hyphenated to preserve the bird-egg-product.
Loanword (Persian/Akkadian); fortified palace/citadel (Susa, temple-citadel); the hyphenated English marks the type.

Original concordant: house-of-construction-separate-part. Eze-the-breadth-of-the-side-rooms-of-the-house and Job-his-roots-are-wrapped-around-a-stone-heap-he-sees-the-house-of-stones and Job-how-much-more-in-them-that-dwell-in-houses-of-clay (Eze 41:9; Job 8:17; 4:19).
Root bnh (H1129). Bayit is the built: structure, lineage, or place. One Hebrew word, one English equivalent.
Aramaic; concordantly identical to H1004 bayit Hebrew ('house') with language-marker.
Proper noun ('house') Moabite place of lamentation; Isa 15:2; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bayith.
Place-name 'house-of-El'; concordantly transliterated as proper noun.
Proper noun, city destroyed by Shalman; Hos 10:14; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beth-Arbel.

Original concordant: Beth-Baal-Meon-city-Reuben-Transjordan. Josh-and-Beth-Baal-Meon and 1Chr-Bela-son-Azaz-son-Shema-son-Joel-who-dwelt-in-Aroer-to-Nebo-to-Baal-Meon (Josh 13:17; 1Chr 5:8 cf). Hyphenated.
Proper noun ('my-spring-house') Simeon-city; 1Chr 4:31; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beth-Biri.
Proper noun, place established by Hareph; 1Chr 2:51; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beth-Gader.
Proper noun ('recompense-house') Moab-city smitten; Jer 48:23; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beth-Gamul.
Proper noun ('house-two-fig-cakes') Moab-city smitten; Jer 48:22; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beth-Diblathaim.
Patronym-clan Bethel-inhabitant Hiel; 1Kgs 16:34; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bethelite.
Proper noun ('side-house') place of Mic-lamentation; Mic 1:11; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beth-ha-Ezel.
Reuben-city and Moab-border-place near Dead-Sea (Num 33:49; Josh 12:3; 13:20; Eze 25:9). Compound 'house-of-wastelands'.
Proper noun ('vineyard-house') signal-place Jerusalem; Jer 6:1; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beth-Hakkerem.
Designation of inhabitants of Bethlehem (1Sam 16:1,18; 17:58; 2Sam 21:19). Gentilic; family with H1035 Beth-Lechem.
Proper noun ('far-off-house') David's-flight-stop; 2Sam 15:17; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beth-Merhaq.

Original concordant: Beth-ha-Markaboth-city-Simeon-Negev. Josh-Bethsor-Shema-Bether-Beth-Lebaoth-Sharuhen-thirteen-cities and 1Chr-Beth-Markaboth-Hazar-Susim-Beth-Biri-Shaaraim-these-were-their-cities-until-David-became-king (Josh 19:5 cf; 1Chr 4:31). Hyphenated.
Proper noun ('house-of-the-valley') Asher-city; Josh 19:27; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beth-Emek.
Beth-Arabah-Jordan-valley-place in Judah-Benjamin-border (Josh 15:6,61; 18:18,22). English convention: Beth-Arabah. 'House-of-the-wilderness-plain' (at-Jordan-valley).
Proper noun, Gad-city; Josh 13:27; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beth-haram.
Proper noun, place of Gad-tribe; Num 32:36; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beth-haran.
Proper noun, place to which Midianites fled; Judg 7:22; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beth-shittah.
Beth-Hoglah-border-place Benjamin-Judah (Josh 15:6; 18:19,21). English convention: Beth-Hoglah. 'House-of-partridge' or 'house-of-the-twirler'.
Proper noun ('hollow-house'); Benjamite/Ephraimite city-pairs (Upper and Lower) on important strategic pass; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun ('house-of-the-pasture') place of Mizpah-victory; 1Sam 7:11; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beth-car.
Proper noun ('house-of-lionesses') Simeon-city; Josh 19:6; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beth-lebaoth.
Proper noun ('bread-house'); city in Judah; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun ('dust-house') Mic-places-lamentation; Mic 1:10; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beth-Leaphrah.

Original concordant: Beth-Maacah-Abel-city-north. 2S-they-besieged-him-in-Abel-Beth-Maacah-and-they-cast-up-a-rampart-against-the-city and 1K-he-smote-Abel-Beth-Maacah-and-all-Chinneroth-with-the-whole-land-of-Naphtali (2S 20:14; 1K 15:20 cf). Hyphenated.

Original concordant: Beth-nimrah-city-Gad-Transjordan. Num-sons-Gad-built-Beth-Nimrah-Beth-Haran and Josh-Beth-Haran-and-Beth-Nimrah-Succoth-Zaphon-rest-of-kingdom-of-Sihon (Num 32:36; Josh 13:27). Hyphenated.
Proper noun, origin-place returnees Benjamin; Neh 7:28; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beth-Azmaveth.
Proper noun, Judah-hill-country-city; Josh 15:59; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beth-anoth.
Beth-Anath-city in Naphtali where Canaanites-remain-living (Josh 19:38; Judg 1:33; 1Chr 4:19). English convention: Beth-Anath. 'House-of-Anath' (Canaanite-goddess-Anath-toponym).

Original concordant: Beth-Pelet-city-Judah-south-Negev. Josh-Beth-Pelet-Hazar-shual and Neh-sons-Judah-settled-in-Dibon-Jekabzeel-villages-Jeshua-Moladah-Beth-Pelet (Josh 15:27; Neh 11:26). Hyphenated.
Moab-sanctuary of Baal-Peor and grave of Moses (Deut 3:29; 4:46; 34:6; Josh 13:20). Compound 'house-of-Peor'; family with H6465 Pe'or.
Proper noun, Issachar-city; Josh 19:21; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beth-pazzez.
Judah-city and Caleb-descendant in hill-country (Josh 15:58; Neh 3:16; 1Chr 2:45; 2Chr 11:7). Compound 'house-of-the-rock'; family with H6697 tsur.
Proper noun, son of Eshton-Judah-branch; 1Chr 4:12; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beth-rapha.
Canaanite-Philistine city in the Jordan-valley (Josh 17:11,16; Judg 1:27; 1Sam 31:10,12; 2Sam 21:12; 1Kgs 4:12; 1Chr 7:29). English convention: Beth-Shean.
Proper noun ('house-of-the-sun'); city in Judah/Naphtali; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun ('house-of-the-apple') Judah-city; Josh 15:53; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beth-tappuah.

Original concordant: palace-house-pavilion-pleasure-pavilion. Esther-royal-palace-pavilion and Persian-court-company and royal-garden-pavilion (Esth 1:5; 7:7,8). Hyphenated to distinguish the palace-house-pavilion-aspect from H1004 bayit.
Proper noun ('weeping-valley') where pilgrims pass through; Ps 84:6; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Baca.
Valley-trees through which David's army-ritual (2Sam 5:23,24; 1Chr 14:14,15; Ps 84:7). Hyphenated to distinguish the balsam-mulberry-aspect from H8256 shiqmah 'sycamore' (already assigned).
Root bkh. 'Weep' preserves the lament-cry-kernel; 'cry' is English synonym, 'weep' is the concordant choice for tears-shedding.
People-wept great-weeping during confession Ezra; Ezra 10:1.
Root bkr (be-firstborn, H1069). 'Firstborn' preserves the ordinal position.
From √bakar (be-firstborn); first yield of harvest offered (Pentecost); the hyphenated English marks position (distinguished from bechor 'firstborn').
From √bachar (be-first); right and prerogative of firstborn (Esau, Reuben); the hyphenated English marks juridical status.
Proper noun, ancestor of Saul; 1Sam 9:1; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bekorath.
From √bachah (cry); loud tears as expression of grief; concordantly 'weeping'.
Proper noun ('weepers') where the angel rebuked the people; Judg 2:5; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bochim.
Eldest-daughter specifically female (Gen 19:31,33,34,37; 29:26; 1Sam 14:49). Hyphenated to distinguish female-firstborn from H1060 bekor 'firstborn' (male-generic).
Firstling-right give or early-fruits (Lev 27:26; Deut 21:16; Eze 47:12; Job 15:32). Hyphenated to distinguish the firstborn-aspect from H3205 yalad 'bear' and H7069 qanah 'acquire'.
Benjamin's son and Ephraimite family-name (Gen 46:21; Num 26:35; 1Chr 7:6,8). 'Young-camel'. English convention: Becher.
Aramean city on the northern border (2Sam 20:14,15; 1Kgs 15:20; 2Kgs 15:29). English convention: Beth-Maacah.
Patronym-clan son of Ephraim; Num 26:35; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bachrite.
Poetic negation-particle; synonym with lo; concordantly 'not' (same negation).
Bel-Babylon's-chief-god-is-put-to-shame and Bel-bows-down-Nebo-stoops and Bel-falls-over-Jeremiah (Isa 46:1; Jer 50:2; 51:44). English convention: Bel. Babylonian-chief-god-equivalent-Baal.
Original concordant: heart-consideration-aramaic. Aramaic parallel to bal; king-set-heart on rescue-Daniel; Dan 6:14.
Reviving-brightening at distress and turning-anger-away (Job 9:27; 10:20; Amos 5:9; Ps 39:14). Hyphenated to distinguish the brighten-revive-aspect from H2896 tov 'be-good' and H8055 samach.
Bilgah-fifteenth-priestly-division-David and Bilgah-priest-family-returnee (1Chr 24:14; Neh 12:5,18). English convention: Bilgah. 'Refreshment-cheerfulness' (family with balag 'brighten').
Proper noun, priestly signatory of covenant Nehemiah; Neh 10:8; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bilgai.
Second friend of Job from Shuah (Job 2:11; 8:1; 18:1; 25:1; 42:9). English convention: Bildad. 'Lord-of-Adad'.
Qal/Piel: wear away, grow old (clothes, generations), cause to age (God makes enemies pass away); concordantly 'wear-out'.
Old worn-out sacks or clothes (Josh 9:4,5; Jer 38:11,12; Eze 23:43). Hyphenated to preserve the worn-out-aspect; family with H1086 balah.
Proper noun, Simeon-city; Josh 19:3; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Balah.

Rachel's-handmaid given as concubine to Jacob, mother of Dan and Naphtali (Gen 29:29 Laban's-gift, 30:3-7 two sons through her bear-on-Rachel's-knees, 35:22 Reuben's-incest-with-her, 35:25, 37:2 Joseph).
Second-sense Bilhah as place; Simeon-city; 1Chr 4:29; concordantly transliterated.

Abstract-noun for-sudden-terror-with-destruction distinguished from H4288 mechittah (terror) by total-destruction-aspect (Job 18:11,14 Bildad-on-the-wicked, 24:17, 27:20, 30:15, Isa 17:14, Jer 51:55, Eze 26:21, 27:36).
Horite-descendant and Benjamite (Gen 36:27; 1Chr 1:42; 7:10). English convention: Bilhan. 'Their-admiration'.
Jer-under-your-armpits-between-cords-worn-rags-Jeremiah-pulled-out-of-pit (Jer 38:11,12 twice). Hyphenated to distinguish the rags-worn-piece-aspect from H5499 sechavah-tatter.

Original concordant: proper-name-Belteshazzar-Daniel-aramaic-name. Proper noun Belteshazzar, court-name of Daniel (Akkadian Balatsu-usur 'protect his life') - in Daniel 1:7 (the chief of the eunuchs gave them names; Daniel he called Belteshazzar) and Daniel 10:1.
Daniel's Babylonian court-name, in honour of Baal-protector (Dan 1:7; 2:26; 4:5,6,15,16; 5:12; 10:1). English convention: Belteshazzar. Concordantly via '-aramaic'.
Negation-particle: without, not; concordantly 'without' (distinguished from lo/ayin).
Original concordant: mixed-fodder-grain-mixture-cattle-feed. Job-wild-ass-mixed-fodder and Job-ox-at-his-feed-trough-mixture and Isa-grain-mixed-fodder (Job 6:5; 24:6; Isa 30:24). Hyphenated.
God hangs the earth on-nothing; Job 26:7.
Compound form (beli + yaal) 'without profit'; lawlessness, in NT 'Belial'; concordantly 'worthlessness'.
Qal: stir together (flour with oil, languages); concordantly 'mix'.
Hapax Judg 19:21 donkeys-feed-mixed; sub-sense pair with H1101a mix.
Hapax Ps 32:9 horse-harness-restrain; cognate H5716 adi ornament.
Qal: gulp down/engulf; distinguished from bala II (communicate); concordantly 'swallow-up'.

Swallowing or engulfing as action - in Psalm 52:6 (you love all devouring words, O deceitful tongue) and Jeremiah 51:44 (I will bring forth out of his mouth that which he has swallowed up); abstract noun.
Proper noun; older name of Zoar, and king in Edom, and Benjamite; concordantly transliterated (distinguished from bela 'swallowing').
Patronym-clan son of Benjamin; Num 26:38; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Belaite.
Proper noun (probably 'not-people' or 'devourer'); prophet of Beor; concordantly transliterated.
Second-sense Bileam as place; Levi-city of Manasseh; 1Chr 6:70; concordantly transliterated.

Lay waste and empty - in Isaiah 24:1 (the LORD makes the earth empty and makes it waste, and turns it upside down) and Nahum 2:11 (the city is empty and laid waste); reduplication-formula baqaq bilqah.
Proper noun; king of Moab; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun, Babylonian king; Dan 8:1; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Belshazzar.
Persian loanword 'treasurer/keeper-of-funds' in Daniel (Dan 3:2,3). Hyphenated to preserve the official-function; concordantly via '-aramaic'.
One of the twelve leaders who returned with Zerubbabel from Babel - Ezra 2:2, Nehemiah 7:7.
Negative particle, specifically with infinitive-constructions. 'Not-' with hyphen preserves the prefixal function; distinguished from lo (H3808) and al (H408).
Unique lexeme. Elevation, hilltop, cultic high-place. 'High-place' covers the physical and cultic meaning.
Proper noun-question 'what is-that-high-place' wordplay-bamah; Eze 20:29; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun, Asher tribe-head son of Japhlet; 1Chr 7:33; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bimhal.
Poetic-archaic length-form of preposition be- (in/with/by); Job 9:30 'with snow-water', 16:4 'with words', 19:16 'with mouth', 20:23 'in his belly', 37:8, 38:16, 40:13, Ps 11:2 'in darkness', 18.
Moabite offering-height on exodus-route (Num 21:19,20; 22:41; Josh 13:17). English convention: Bamoth. 'Heights'; family with H1116 bamah 'high-place' (already assigned).
Root bnh (build, H1129). Ben is the built-one in the lineage; female parallel bat (H1323).
Aramaic-coloured variant of ben (son) in the Chronicles-genealogies, related to H1121a ben (son); main-form occurs in 1Chr 15:18, 2Chr 5:2 and similar register-passages.
Proper noun, Levi-singer ('son-of-Asaph'); 1Chr 15:18; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ben.

Aramaic-cognate of-Hebrew-H1121a ben (son) distinguished by Aramaic-language-form in-Daniel-and-Ezra (Dan 3:25 fiery-furnace-rescue-witness 'lo I-see four-men-loose walking in-the-midst-of-the-fire').
Aramaic verb: erect (temple, wall); parallel to Hebrew banah; concordantly 'build-aramaic'.
Proper noun ('son-of-my-sorrow') Rachel's name for Benjamin; Gen 35:18; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ben-oni.
Root bnh. Stem-family: bayit (house, H1004b), ben (son, H1121a). 'Build' is kernel-activity.
Proper noun ('son-of-Hadad'); title of Aramean kings of Damascus; concordantly transliterated.
Post-exilic Levites and family-heads (Ezra 8:33; 10:30,38; Neh 3:24; 7:15; 10:10; 12:8). 'Building'. English convention: Binnui.
Proper noun, son of Ishi-Judah-branch; 1Chr 4:20; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ben-zoheth.
Proper noun, Jehoshaphat's prince for teaching; 2Chr 17:7; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ben-hail.
Proper noun, son of Shimon-Judah-branch; 1Chr 4:20; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ben-hanan.
Proper noun; various Levites and returnees from exile (Ezra, Nehemiah); concordantly transliterated.
Bunni-Levite-Nehemiah-assembly and Bunni-sealer-covenant-renewal and Bunni-Levite-post-exile-house (Neh 9:4; 10:16; 11:15). English convention: Bunni. 'My-builder' or 'built' (family with banah).
Proper noun, Dan-city ('sons-of-the-lightning'); Josh 19:45; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bene-berak.
Proper noun ('YHWH-built'); chief of David's bodyguard; concordantly transliterated.
Gentilic-designation 'son-of-the-right-hand-tribe'; Saul and later Mordecai (1Sam 9:1,21; 2Sam 16:11; 19:17; 20:1; 1Kgs 2:8; Ps 7:1; Esth 2:5). Derivative of H1144 Binyamin.
Eze-building-on-southside and Eze-construction-broad-five-cubits and Eze-building-separated-place (Eze 40:5; 41:12,15; 42:1,5,10). Hyphenated.
Proper noun, Levi-signatory of covenant Nehemiah; Neh 10:13; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beninu.
Proper noun ('son-of-my-people') son of Lot; Gen 19:38; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ben-ammi.
Father of Meshullam-wall-builder Neh 3:6; theophoric proper noun (in-counsel-Yah).
Head of a Nethinim-family in the return-list - Ezra 2:49, Nehemiah 7:52; disambiguated from H1209 Besai (Joab-son).
Original concordant: unripe-grape-unripe-fruit-sour-grapes. Unripe-fruit as fathers-sin-image (Isa 18:5; Jer 31:29,30; Eze 18:2; Job 15:33). Hyphenated.
Aramaic verb 'seek/request' in Daniel and Ezra (Ezra 7:14; Dan 2:13,16,18,23,49; 4:33; 6:4,7,12,13; 7:16). Concordantly linked via '-aramaic' to Hebrew H1245 baqash.
Preposition. Through-for, in-favour-of, via. 'On-behalf-of' preserves the mediation-intent; 'for' is too generic.
Thoroughly-investigate or boil-up-bubble (Isa 21:12; 30:13; 64:1,2; Obad 1:6). Hyphenated to distinguish the inquire-search-aspect from H1875 darash 'inquire' and H2713 chaqar 'search-out'.

Original concordant: petition-supplication-prayer-aramaic. Aramaic word for petition or supplication - in Daniel 6:7 (whoever shall ask a petition of any god or man for thirty days) and Daniel 6:13 (Daniel prays his prayer); from beah (ask, seek).
Father of prophet-seer-for-hire Balaam (Num 22:5, 24:3,15, 31:8 killed-with-Midianites, Deut 23:5, Josh 13:22, 24:9, Mic 6:5); also father of Bela, first king.
The terrors which God's arrows cause in Job - Job 6:4 (the terrors of God set themselves in array against me) and Psalm 88:17 (Your terrors render me speechless); from H1204 baath (terrify).
Proper noun; husband of Ruth, ancestor of David, also temple-pillar; concordantly transliterated.
Hapax Job 30:24 on-rubble-heap-not-stretch-out-hand; from H1165 baah inquire-dig.
Pack-livestock in household or caravan (Gen 45:17; Ex 22:4; Num 20:4,8,11; Ps 78:48). Hyphenated; distinguishes transport-or-work-cattle from H929 behemah 'beast' (animal-general).
Qal: be husband, become master over; the hyphenated English marks position (distinguished from baal noun 'lord' and Baal pn).
Function-term: owner/responsible-one; the hyphenated English preserves authority + ownership; person-name Baal = H1168a.
Proper noun; god of Canaan; concordantly transliterated because proper-nouns are not translated.

Reubenite family-ancestor and Benjamite-Gibeonite (1Chr 5:5; 8:30; 9:36). English convention: Baal-person. Distinguished from homonym H1168a baal 'Baal-god' (already assigned); family with H1167 baal.
Baal-Gad-valley-northern-border-Lebanon and Joshua-border-marker (Josh 11:17; 12:7; 13:5). English convention: Baal-Gad. 'Lord-of-fortune' (Canaanite-Gad-deity-toponym).
Female-owner or ruler-woman (1Sam 28:7 twice; Nah 3:4; Isa 47:7). Hyphenated to distinguish the mistress-owner-aspect from H1404 geveret 'mistress' (already assigned); family with H1167 ba'al.
Kiriath-Jearim also called Baalah (Josh 15:9,10,11,29; 1Chr 13:6). English convention: Baalah. 'Mistress'. Distinguished from homonym H1172 ba'alah 'mistress-woman'.
Proper noun, Solomon-vineyard-location; Song 8:11; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Baal-hamon.
Proper noun, Judah-city south; Josh 15:24; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bealoth.
Philistine Ekron-god whom Ahaziah consults (2Kgs 1:2,3,6,16). English convention: Baal-Zebub. Compound 'lord-of-flies'; family with H2070 zevuv 'fly'.
Proper noun, place where Absalom killed Amnon; 2Sam 13:23; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Baal-Hazor.
Proper-noun-title ('my-master') forbidden for YHWH; Hos 2:16; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Baali.
Proper noun, David's-son Jerusalem-born variant Eliada; 1Chr 14:7; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beeliada.
Proper noun, Benjamite David's-warrior Ziklag; 1Chr 12:5; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bealiah.
Proper noun ('Judah-burghers') where David fetched the ark; 2Sam 6:2; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Baale-Judah.
Proper noun, Ammonite king who sent Ishmael-against-Gedaliah; Jer 40:14; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Baalis.
Baal-Meon-city in Reuben-territory and Moab-lament (Num 32:38; 1Chr 5:8; Eze 25:9). English convention: Baal-Meon. 'Lord-of-dwelling' (Canaanite-toponym-combination).
Moabite idol with whose cult Israel committed harlotry (Num 25:3,5; Deut 4:3; Ps 106:28; Hos 9:10). English convention: Baal-Peor; compound with H1168 Baal.
Place-name of David's breakthrough against the Philistines (2Sam 5:20 twice; 1Chr 14:11 twice; Isa 28:21). Compound 'Baal-of-breakings'; family with H6555 parats 'break-through'.
Baal-Zephon-toponym at Pi-hahiroth and Egyptian-border (Ex 14:2,9; Num 33:7). English convention: Baal-Zephon. 'Lord-of-the-North' (Canaanite-storm-god-toponym).
Proper noun, place of origin of firstfruit-loaves Elisha; 2Kgs 4:42; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Baal-Shalishah.
Baalath-city in Dan-territory and rebuilt-by-Solomon (Josh 19:44; 1Kgs 9:18; 2Chr 8:6). English convention: Baalath. 'Female-Baal-goddess' or 'mistress-city'.
Proper noun ('mistress-of-the-well') Simeon-city; Josh 19:8; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Baalath-Beer.
Proper noun ('palm-lord') battle-place Benjamin-war; Judg 20:33; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Baal-Tamar.
Proper noun, place of Gad-inheritance; Num 32:3; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beon.
Different persons: murderer of Ish-bosheth, mighty man of David, overseer of Solomon (2Sam 4:2,5,6,9; 23:29; 1Kgs 4:12,16; 1Chr 11:30; Ezra 2:2; Neh 3:4; 7:7; 10:28). English convention: Baanah.
Root b'r. 'Burn' preserves the fire-active; 'consume-by-fire' is transitive splinter.
Second homonym distinguished from ba'ar-I (burn, H1197a); Qal/Piel/Hiphil: by-cattle-or-fire-consume-bare distinguished from ra'ah-I (pasture, H7462a) by exhausting-consumption-aspect (Ex 22:4 etc.).
Beast-like illiterate man (Ps 49:11; 73:22; 92:7; 94:8; Prov 12:1; 30:2). Hyphenated to distinguish the brutish-stupid-aspect from H3684 kesil 'fool' and H5036 naval 'fool-godless'.
Proper noun, wife of Shaharaim whom he sent away; 1Chr 8:8; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Baara.
Proper noun; king of the Northern Kingdom; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun, Gershon-Levi-genealogy descendant Asaph; 1Chr 6:40; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Baaseiah.
Proper noun, Levi-city of Manasseh; Josh 21:27; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beeshterah.
Piel: suddenly terrify (nightly anxiety, evil spirit upon Saul); the hyphenated English marks the sudden-onset.
Marshy salt-lands and water-pool (Job 8:11; 40:21; Eze 47:11). Hyphenated to distinguish the marsh-pool-aspect from H98 agam 'pool-marsh' and H4325 mayim 'water' (already assigned).

Bezai-temple-servants-family-head-returnees-Zerubbabel-and-Ezra-and-Nehemiah-lists (Ezra 2:49; Neh 7:52; 10:19). English convention: Bezai. 'Conqueror' or 'treader' (etymology-uncertain-possibly-family-with batsa).
Plucking and pressing grapes as annual harvest-festival (Lev 26:5; Judg 8:2; Isa 24:13; 32:10; Jer 48:32; 49:9; Mic 7:1; Zech 11:2). Hyphenated to mark pluck-season; family with H1219 batsar.

Theophoric-name 'in shadow-of-El' - chief-craftsman of-the-tribe-Judah for Tabernacle-making (Ex 31:2 'I-have-called-by-name Bezalel son-of-Uri son-of-Hur of-tribe-Judah; I-have-filled-him-with-Spirit').
Head of a Nethinim-family in the return-list - Ezra 2:52, Nehemiah 7:54.
Qal/Piel: cut-off for oneself, practise rapacity (Proverbs, Ezekiel); the hyphenated English marks motive.
Deut-your-clothing-did-not-grow-old-on-you and Neh-and-the-feet-of-them-did-not-swell and Ex-and-the-people-took-their-dough-before-it-was-leavened (Deut 8:4; Neh 9:21; Ex 12:34 cf). Hyphenated.
Unbaked dough-mass for bread (Ex 12:34,39; 2Sam 13:8; Jer 7:18; Hos 7:4). Hyphenated to distinguish the kneading-mass-aspect from H3888 lush 'dough-knead' (verb).
Original concordant: Bozkath-city-Judah-Shephelah. Josh-Lachish-Bozkath-Eglon and 2K-the-name-of-his-mother-was-Jedidah-the-daughter-of-Adaiah-of-Bozkath (Josh 15:39; 2K 22:1). Hyphenated.
Qal: harvest grapes, cut off; Niphal: be inaccessible (walls, fortress); the hyphenated English covers both semantic axes.
The gold-ore or precious metal in raw form - Job 22:24 (lay your gold to dust) and 36:19 (not gold nor all the strong-resources); to be distinguished from refined gold.
Reubenite city-of-refuge in plateau (Deut 4:43; Josh 20:8; 21:36; 1Chr 6:63,78). English convention: Bezer. 'Inaccessible-stronghold-city'.
Capital/fortified-city in Edom (Gen 36:33; 1Chr 1:44; Isa 34:6; 63:1; Jer 48:24; 49:13,22; Amos 1:12; Mic 2:12). From batsar 'make-impregnable'. English convention: Bozrah.
Head of a Nethinim-family in the return-list, name means flask/jug - Ezra 2:51, Nehemiah 7:53.
Original concordant: flask-bottle-earthen-jar-stop-jar. Jeroboam's-wife-flask-honey-for-prophet and Jeremiah's-symbolic-jar-breaking (1Kgs 14:3; Jer 19:1,10). Hyphenated.
Bakbukiah-Levite-second-in-rank-Nehemiah and Bakbukiah-gatekeeper-temple-gates and Bakbukiah-ancestor-priestly-line (Neh 11:17; 12:9,25). English convention: Bakbukiah.
Proper noun, Levi tribe-head post-exile; 1Chr 9:15; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bakbakkar.
Aaronite priest and Danite prince (Num 34:22; 1Chr 5:31; 6:36; Ezra 7:4). English convention: Bukki. 'My-pouring-out'.
One of the sons of Heman, levitical temple-musician and head of the sixth division - 1Chronicles 25:4, 25:13.

Original concordant: breach-cleft-crack-in-wall. Crack or breach in wall - in Isaiah 22:9 (the breaches of the city of David you saw) and Amos 6:11 (He shall smite the great house with breaches); from H1234 baqa (split).
Qal: cut through, break open (rock, sea, egg); concordantly 'split'.
Aramaic parallel to biqah; plain-of-Dura; Dan 3:1.
From √baqa (split); valley between mountains; the hyphenated English marks geography.
Empty-pour or strip-bare of city or heart (Isa 19:3; 24:1,3; Jer 19:7; 51:2; Nah 2:3). Hyphenated to distinguish the emptying-strip-aspect from H7324 ruq 'pour-out'.
Carefully examine, inspect cattle or priestly-examination (Lev 13:36; 27:33; 2Kgs 16:15; Ps 27:4; Prov 20:25; Eze 34:11,12). Hyphenated; distinguishes inspection-inquiry from homonym H1241 baqar.

Original concordant: inquire-search-investigate-aramaic. Investigate-in-empire-archives-chronicles and in-treasury-of-Babel-search and king-decree-by-law-investigate (Ezra 4:15,19; 5:17; 6:1; 7:14). Hyphenated.
Unique lexeme. Collective for cattle. 'Cattle' covers the large-livestock; distinguished from tson (small-livestock, H6629).
Root bqr (inquire, H1239). Morning as time-of-discernment (light/dark). 'Morning' standard.
Root bqsh. Piel-intensively seek. 'Seek' is kernel.

What-is-asked/requested; petition especially in Esther and post-exile (Ezra 7:6; Esth 5:3,6,7,8; 7:2,3; 9:12). Hyphenated; distinguishes formal-court-petition from H8467 techinnah supplication and H8605.
Aramaic 'son-of' in genealogies and royal-title (Ezra 5:1,2; 6:14; Ps 2:12 (?); Dan 3:25; 5:22; 7:13). Hyphenated to preserve distinction from homonym H1247b 'field-aramaic'; family with H1121.

Original concordant: royal-son-firstborn-noble-son. Honorific-use 'son' with king and wisdom-address (Ps 2:12; Prov 31:2 three times). Hyphenated to distinguish the royal-son-noble-aspect from homonyms H1247 bar-Aram-II 'son-aramaic' (already assigned).
Moral-ritual purity of heart or deed (Job 11:4; 33:9; Ps 24:4; 73:1; Prov 14:4; Song 6:9,10). Hyphenated to preserve inward-purity; family with H1305 barar 'purify'.
Open-field grain (Gen 41-42, Joseph's stores), corn on the threshing-floor; the hyphenated English distinguishes from bar II 'son-aramaic' and III 'pure'.
Second-sense bar; mountain-goat-bears young in-field; Job 39:4.
Aramaic-equivalent for outside-field (Dan 2:38; 4:9,12,20,22,29,30). Hyphenated to mark the Aramaic-parallel; distinguished from Hebrew H7704 sadeh 'field'.
Moral pure-state of hands or heart (2Sam 22:21,25; Ps 18:21,25; Job 22:30). Hyphenated to distinguish the innocence-purity-aspect from H2890 tohar 'cleanness' and H5355 naqi 'innocent'.
The cleanness of hands by which God recompenses - Psalm 18:21 (He has rewarded me according to the cleanness of my hands), 2Samuel 22:21, Job 22:30; from H1249 bar (pure-clean).
Qal: unique divine creating (only God as subject); distinguished from yatsar (form) and asah (make); concordantly 'create'.
Second-sense bara; Eli's sons gorge-themselves with sacrifice-meat; 1Sam 2:29.
Proper noun, Babylonian king after Hezekiah's-recovery; 2Kgs 20:12; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Berodach-baladan.
Proper noun, Benjamin-son Shimei; 1Chr 8:21; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beraiah.
Ice-precipitation from storm, plague in Egypt; concordantly 'hail'.
Pepper-salt colour-pattern of Laban-flock (Gen 31:10,12; Zech 6:3,6). Hyphenated to distinguish the spotted-spotted-aspect from H5348 naqod 'speckled' (already assigned) and H5921 talu 'spotted'.
Mourn-meal or strength-food consume (2Sam 3:35; 12:17; 13:5,6,10; Lam 4:10). Hyphenated to preserve the comfort-food-aspect; family with H1279 biryah 'food-dish'.
Proper noun ('blessed'); scribe of Jeremiah; concordantly transliterated.
Conifer of Lebanon, used for temple-construction; the hyphenated English marks species.
First-sense Berothah; northern border-place Israel; Eze 47:16; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Berothah.
Second-sense Berothai; Aramean place David-spoils; 2Sam 8:8; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Berothai.
