Gileadite from-Rogelim who-fed David's-fugitive-company at-Jordan-crossing (2Sam 17:27-29 David-at-Mahanaim, 19:32-40 Barzillai's-elderly-decline-of-honour, 1Kgs 2:7 David's-deathbed-charge-Solomon-honour).
Qal: run away from, escape; concordantly 'flee-away' (distinguished from nus = flee).
Patronym-clan David's-warrior Azmaveth; 2Sam 23:31; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Barhumite.
Proper noun, Asher tribe-head son of Zophah (not H1276 tribe-Beri); 1Chr 7:36; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beri.
Proper noun, people in Abel-region; 2Sam 20:14; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beri.
From √bara (be-thick); fat and healthy (fat cows of Pharaoh, fat flock); concordantly 'well-fleshed'.
Something-completely-new; earth swallows up Korah; Num 16:30.
Cross-beam that bars gate or door; concordantly 'bar'.
Leviathan-fleeing-twisting-serpent and Isa-leviathan-fleeing-serpent and Jer-Babel-flee-as-serpent (Job 26:13; Isa 27:1; 43:14). Hyphenated.
Proper noun, son of Shemaiah-David-branch; 1Chr 3:22; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bariah.
Son of Asher, grandson of Jacob (Gen 46:17, Num 26:44-45, 1Chr 7:30-31); son of Ephraim (1Chr 7:23); Levitical main-line (1Chr 23:10-11); Benjamite (1Chr 8:13-16); concordantly transliterated.
Patronym-clan son of Asher; Num 26:44; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beriite.
Unique lexeme. Etymology contested (possibly brh = cut). Legally binding agreement. 'Covenant' standard.
Proper noun, Shechem-deity ('covenant-El'); Judg 9:46; concordantly transliterated. English convention: El-berith.

Lye or potash as detergent - in Jeremiah 2:22 (though you wash yourself with lye and use much soap) and Malachi 3:2 (He is like the refiner's fire and like the fullers' soap); alkaline cleaning agent.
Root brk. Piel-directed action of speaking-prosperity. Derived berakhah (blessing, H1293). 'Bless' is kernel-meaning.
Aramaic-equivalent for kneeling-blessing of God (Dan 2:19,20; 3:28; 4:31; 6:11). Hyphenated to mark the Aramaic-parallel; family with H1288 barakh 'bless' (Hebrew).
Body-part, seat of bowing and blessing-gesture; concordantly 'knee'.
Aramaic parallel to berek; Daniel-on-knees three-times-daily; Dan 6:10.
The father of the young wise-man Elihu of the family Buzi of Aram - Job 32:2, 32:6; name means 'God has blessed'.
From √barach (kneel/bless); the blessing as gift or utterance; concordantly 'blessing'.
Beracah-valley-where-Jehoshaphat-people-blessed-YHWH-after-victory-Moab-Ammon-Edom (2Chr 20:26 twice). English convention: Beracah-valley. Distinguished from H1293 berakhah 'blessing'.
Walled pond (Siloam, Bethesda, Gibeon); the hyphenated English marks function (distinguished from berachah 'blessing').
Various Levites and Zerubbabel-contemporary (1Chr 3:20; 6:24,39; 9:16; 15:17,23; 2Chr 28:12; Neh 3:4,30; 6:18; Zech 1:1,7). 'YHWH-blesses'. English convention: Berekiah.

Original concordant: but-however-yet-nevertheless-aramaic. Aramaic-contrast in vision or decree (Ezra 5:13; Dan 2:28; 4:12,20,23; 5:17; 7:28). Hyphenated to distinguish the but-however-aspect from H61 aval 'verily' (already assigned); Aramaic cognate.
Proper noun, king of Sodom; Gen 14:2; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bera.
Qal-imperative; cast-lightning and scatter enemies; Ps 144:6.

Original concordant: lightning-arrow-arrow-shot-glitter. 2S-He-sent-arrows-and-scattered-them-lightnings-and-discomfited-them and Ps-He-sent-out-his-arrows-and-scattered-them-and-many-lightnings-and-discomfited-them (2S 22:15; Ps 18:15). Hyphenated.
Flashing heaven-spark, glance of sword; concordantly 'lightning' (distinguished from Baraq-pn).
Proper noun ('lightning'); judge of Naphtali, captain with Deborah against Sisera; concordantly transliterated (distinguished from baraq-noun 'lightning').
Head of a Nethinim-family in the return-list - Ezra 2:53, Nehemiah 7:55.
Qal/Niphal: make pure, sift, choose-out; concordantly 'purify'.
Proper noun, king of Gomorrah; Gen 14:2; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Birsha.
Patronym-clan David's-warrior Naharai; 1Chr 11:39; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Berothite.
Besor-brook where David's-weary-men-stayed (1Sam 30:9,10,21). English convention: Besor. 'Cool-brook' or 'good-stream'.
Good message of victory or royal favour (2Sam 4:10; 18:20,22,25,27; 2Kgs 7:9). Hyphenated to preserve the joyful-tidings-aspect; family with H1319 basar 'bring-good-news'.
Piel: bring food to readiness in water; distinguished from tsalah (roast) and afah (bake); concordantly 'boil'.
From √basam (smell pleasantly); fragrant spice, balsam; the hyphenated English marks the aromatic load.
Wife of Esau and daughter of Solomon (Gen 26:34; 36:3,4,10,13,17; 1Kgs 4:15). 'Fragrant'. English convention: Basemath.
Proper noun (region east of Jordan); fertile plateau; concordantly transliterated.
Piel: announce victory or salvation, bring-evangel; the hyphenated English distinguishes from basar noun 'flesh'.
Unique lexeme. Anatomical and generic ('all flesh' = all living). 'Flesh' covers both.
Aramaic word for flesh or body - in Daniel 4:12 (of his fruits all flesh was fed) and Daniel 7:5 (devour much flesh); parallel of Hebrew basar.
From √bosh (be-ashamed); the feeling and the cause of shame; concordantly 'shame'.
Root bnh (build, H1129); female counterpart of ben (H1121a). 'Daughter' standard.
Large liquid-measure (about 22 litres), counterpart of ephah for dry measures; the hyphenated English distinguishes from bat 'daughter'.

Original concordant: bath-capacity-measure-aramaic. The bath-capacity-measure for liquids in the Aramaic context - Ezra 7:22 (a hundred baths of wine, a hundred baths of oil); Aramaic cognate of Hebrew bath (about 22 litres).
Son of Nahor and Milcah, nephew-of-Abraham, father-of-Rebekah-and-Laban - link in Patriarch-genealogy (Gen 22:22-23, 24:15,24,47,50, 25:20, 28:2,5).
Second-sense Bethuel as place Simeon-city; 1Chr 4:30; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun, Simeon-city; Josh 19:4; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bethul.
Woman who has not yet had relations; distinguished from naarah (young-woman general); concordantly 'virgin'.
Plural-abstract of betulah (virgin, H1330); state-or-tokens-of-virginity (Lev 21:13 high-priest 'wife in-her-virginity takes', Deut 22:14-15,17,20 'tokens-of-virginity').
Proper noun, Egyptian Pharaoh-daughter wife of Mered; 1Chr 4:18; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bithiah.
Gen-Abram-took-all-the-animals-and-divided-them-in-the-middle and Gen-the-birds-he-did-not-divide and Jer-cut-the-covenant-calf-in-two (Gen 15:10 twice; Jer 34:18). Hyphenated.

Mountains-of-Bether or division-mountains in Song-of-Songs and covenant-sacrifice-pieces Abraham (Gen 15:10; Jer 34:18,19; Song 2:17). English convention: Bether-mountains. 'Divided-pieces' (cleaving-sacrifice).
Proper noun, Cleft-mountains where bride calls to bridegroom; Song 2:17; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bether.
Proper noun Heshbon-gate 'daughter-of-multitudes'; Song 7:4; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bath-rabbim.
Proper noun, region near Mahanaim; 2Sam 2:29; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bithron.
Compound-name 'daughter-of-seven/oath' - wife-of David after-adultery and-death-of Uriah, mother-of-Solomon (2Sam 11:3, 1Kgs 1:11-31, 2:13-19).
Proper noun variant Bathsheba wife of David; 1Chr 3:5; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bath-shua.
Moab is haughty and proud; Isa 16:6.
Swelling-rising of water, pride or God's might (Ex 15:1,21; Job 8:11; 10:16; Eze 47:5). Hyphenated to preserve the physical-swelling-motion; root of H1343 ge'eh 'proud-haughty'.
High-lifted-self-exalting (adjective) (Job 40:11,12; Ps 94:2; 123:4; 140:6; Prov 15:25; 16:19; Isa 2:12; Jer 48:29). Hyphenated to distinguish attitude-quality from H2086 zed 'insolent'.
Proper noun, spy of Gad; Num 13:15; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Geuel.
From √gaah (be-high); proud attitude as sin (positive = majesty); concordantly 'haughtiness'.
From √gaah (be-high); positively exaltation, negatively pride; concordantly 'exaltation'.
Majestic exalted-loftiness of God or sea-waves (Ps 17:10; 68:35; Isa 9:18; 12:5; 26:10; 28:1,3; Job 41:7). Hyphenated to distinguish divine-loftiness from H1346 ga'avah 'pride'.
Our-soul is filled with mocking of proud-men; Ps 123:4.
Root g'l. Family-duty: redeem from debt, slavery, or blood-feud. 'Redeem' preserves the family-juridical loosing-action; 'rescue' clashes with yasha (H3467).
Second homonym of gaal (redeemer H1350); Niphal/Pual/Hithpael/Hiphil: ritual-physical defile/make-unclean with blood or filth (Lam 4:14, Isa 59:3, Mal 1:7,12, Dan 1:8, Zeph 3:1).
Pual-passive; priests who polluted priesthood-covenant; Neh 13:29.
From √gaal (redeem); right and price of kinsman-redemption (Lev 25, Ruth); the hyphenated English marks family-juridical nature.
Vaulted top (back, vault, eyebrow, rim), edge-elevation; the hyphenated English marks the bow-shaped top.
Aramaic; Dan 7:6; parallel to Hebrew gab.
Original concordant: pits-trenches-water-pools-field-lowland-basins. 2K-thus-says-the-LORD-make-this-valley-full-of-trenches and Jer-her-pits-are-filled-with-water (2K 3:16; Jer 14:3). Hyphenated.
Aramaic-specific term for-dug-pit-for-lions - exclusively in Dan 6:8,13,17-18,20-21,24-25,27 'lions-den' into which Daniel-was-cast for-prayer-against-decree of-Darius.
Water-pool or drinking-pool - in Isaiah 30:14 (to take water out of a pit) and Ezekiel 47:11 (the marshy places and her pits); concrete rain-pool in mountain-region.
Qal: be elevated; Hiphil: lift up; negatively: be haughty; the hyphenated English marks state.
1Sam-Saul-tall-of-shoulder-above-people and Ps-righteous-God-exalted and Prov-haughty-pride-of-heart (1Sam 16:7; Ps 138:6; Prov 16:5). Hyphenated.
From √gavah (be-high); elevated dimension, haughtiness; the hyphenated English distinguishes from marom.
Adjective from √gavah; elevated in dimension or status; concordantly 'high'.
Haughty loftiness - in Isaiah 2:11 (the lofty looks of man shall be humbled and the haughtiness of men shall be bowed down) and Isaiah 2:17 (the loftiness of man shall be bowed down).
Unique lexeme. Border or border-region. 'Border-territory' preserves both the line and the adjacent zone; 'border' alone is too narrow.
Female parallel-form of gevul (border-territory, H1366); demarcation-line-or-territory specifically in-inheritance-division (Num 32:33).
Root gbr (be-strong, H1396). Substantively 'mighty-man', adjectivally 'strong'. 'Strong-mighty-man' preserves both fields; 'hero' alone is too narrow, 'strong' too abstract.
From √gavar (be-strong); might-deed/strength-manifestation; the hyphenated English marks 'strength-as-action'.
Aramaic parallel to gevurah; God's-wisdom-and-strength; Dan 2:20.
Front-side-bald of head or clothing (Lev 13:42,43,55). Hyphenated to distinguish front-baldness from H7146 qarachath 'rear-baldness' and H4696 metsach 'forehead'.
Proper noun, Benjamite Jerusalem-inhabitant; Neh 11:8; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gabbai.
Proper noun, place on Assyrian-march-route; Isa 10:31; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gebim.
Large drinking-bowl (Joseph's silver goblet, lamp-cups of menorah); concordantly 'goblet'.
Gen-Jacob-as-lord-over-brothers-Isaac-blesses and Gen-I-have-set-you-lord-over-him (Gen 27:29,37). Hyphenated to distinguish lord-master-ruler-aspect from H113 adon 'lord'.
Commanding-female title, often for mother of reigning king (1Kgs 11:19; 15:13; 2Kgs 10:13; 2Chr 15:16; Jer 13:18; 29:2). Hyphenated to preserve court-power-aspect; family with H1376 gebir.
Border-trace around territory or mountain (Ex 19:12,23; Deut 19:14; Josh 18:20; Zech 9:2). Hyphenated to preserve the border-demarcation-aspect; family with H1366 gevul 'border-territory'.
Proper noun Byblos-city-suppliers Tyre; Eze 27:9; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gebal.
Proper noun, people in coalition against Israel; Ps 83:7; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gebal.
Inhabitant of Gebal-Byblos; Josh 13:5; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Giblite.
Humped mountain-tops or elevated summits - in Psalm 68:16 (why do you leap, you many-peaked mountains?) and 68:17 (the mountain that God desired for his abode); only in plural, from gav-arched-top.
Proper noun ('hill'); city in Benjamin, Levite-city; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun, city founded by Sheva-Caleb; 1Chr 2:49; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gibea.
Rounded elevation, smaller than har (mountain); concordantly 'hill'.
Proper noun ('hill'); city in Benjamin, residence of Saul; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun ('hill-city'); city of the Gibeonites; concordantly transliterated.
Inhabitant of Gibeon, Hivite city (2Sam 21:1,2,3,4,9; Neh 3:7; 1Chr 12:4). Gentilic; family with H1391 Giv'on.
Proper noun, Benjamin-city; Josh 18:28; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gibeath.
Patronym-clan David's-warriors Gibeah-Benjamin; 1Chr 12:3; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gibeathite.
Qal: have the upper hand, show oneself mighty; the hyphenated English marks comparative state.
From √gavar (be-strong); adult male as powerful person; distinguished from ish (man-human); the hyphenated English preserves strength-connotation.
Father of Solomon-officer 1Kgs 4:19; possibly compound with H1127 Ben-Geber.
Aramaic noun: adult man; parallel to Hebrew gever; concordantly compound with language-marker.
Aramaic parallel to gibbor; warriors to bind-men; Dan 3:20.
Proper noun, origin-group of returnees; Ezra 2:20; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gibbar.
Proper noun archangel explains-Daniel-vision; Dan 8:16; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gabriel.
Mistress-over-handmaid; also city-queen as metaphor (Gen 16:4,8,9; 2Kgs 5:3; Ps 123:2; Prov 30:23; Isa 24:2; 47:5,7). Hyphenated to distinguish female-ruler-status from H4436 malkah.
Levitical city in Dan, besieged by Israel (Josh 19:44; 21:23; 1Kgs 15:27; 16:15,17). English convention: Gibbethon.
Flat-built roof as additional living-space; the hyphenated English marks construction.
Original concordant: coriander-white-seed-manna-comparison. Ex-manna-was-as-coriander-seed-white and Num-manna-was-like-coriander-seed (Ex 16:31; Num 11:7). Hyphenated.
Proper noun Babylonian-deity of fortune; Isa 65:11; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gad.
Proper noun (son/tribe of Israel); concordantly transliterated.

Original concordant: treasurer-treasury-keeper-aramaic. Aramaic loanword for treasurer or treasury-keeper - in Daniel 3:2 (the treasurers) and Daniel 3:3 (the treasurers); Persian ganzabara, official at Dura-plain-ceremonial.
Ritual self-cutting at mourning or at Baal-worship (Deut 14:1; 1Kgs 18:28; Jer 5:7; 16:6; 41:5; 47:5; 48:37; Mic 4:14). Hyphenated to mark middle-reflexive action.

Original concordant: hew-down-fell-cut-off-aramaic. Aramaic verb for hewing down or felling - in Daniel 4:14 (hew down this tree) and Daniel 4:23 (hew down this tree); imperative in angel-decree to Nebuchadnezzar-tree.
Jordan-bank-overflowing at high-water (Josh 3:15; 4:18; 1Chr 12:15; Isa 8:7). Hyphenated to distinguish the bank-edge-aspect from H7097 qatseh 'end' and H8193 safah 'edge-lip'.
Armed gang or military detachment; concordantly 'raiding-band'.
Root gdl (be-great, H1431). 'Great' is direct equivalent.
Second-sense gadol as personal-name father of Zabdiel priest; Neh 11:14; concordantly transliterated.
Female abstract of gadol (great, H1419a); state-or-action-of-being-made-great distinguished from godel (greatness-inward, H1433) (2Sam 7:21 = 1Chr 17:19).
Isa-reproaches-they-heard and Zeph-their-reviling-and-mockery and Eze-rebuked-and-reproached (Isa 43:28; 51:7; Zeph 2:8; Eze 5:15). Hyphenated.
Young of goat, edible feast-offering; the hyphenated English marks age.
From pn Gad; member of tribe Gad; the hyphenated English marks ethnicity.
Proper noun, spy of Manasseh; Num 13:11; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gaddi.
Proper noun, spy of Zebulon; Num 13:10; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gaddiel.
Original concordant: grain-stack-haystack-grain-heap. Burning-in-standing-grain-sheaves and Job's-haystack-image (Ex 22:6; Job 5:26; 21:32). Hyphenated.
Hapax Job 21:32 grave-mound-watched; sub-sense pair with H1430a wheat-stack same stack-form.
Root gdl. Stative 'become-great'; causative 'make-great'. 'Become-great' preserves stative kernel; derived gadol (H1419a).
Child-in-growth-stage before adulthood (Gen 26:13; 1Sam 2:26; 2Chr 17:12). Hyphenated to distinguish growing-youth-aspect from H1431 gadal 'become-great' and H5288 na'ar 'youth'.
From √gdl (be-great); abstract noun 'greatness/magnitude' (Deut 3:24 'Your greatness', Eze 31:7 'greatness of branches'); concordantly 'greatness'.
Post-exilic-Nethinim-family-ancestor and Solomon-servant-family-head (Ezra 2:47,56; Neh 7:49,58). English convention: Giddel. 'Made-great'; family with H1431 gadal 'be-great'.
Pre-exilic persons of the same name as the governor (1Chr 25:3,9; Ezra 10:18; Jer 38:1; Zeph 1:1). 'YHWH-is-great'. English convention: Gedaliah; distinguished from H1436b Gedaliah (longer form).
Proper noun ('YHWH-is-great'); governor over Judah after fall of Jerusalem; concordantly transliterated.
Qal/Piel: hew off (horns, tree, idol-image); concordantly 'cut-down'.
Proper noun ('hewer'); judge from Manasseh; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun, place where Israel defeated Benjamin-fugitives; Judg 20:45; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gidom.
Benjamite father of Abidan (Num 1:11; 2:22; 7:60,65; 10:24). English convention: Gideoni. 'Hewer'.
Words of contempt or blasphemy utter (Num 15:30; 2Kgs 19:6,22; Ps 44:17; Isa 37:6,23; Eze 20:27). Hyphenated to mark verbal-reproach.
Qal/Piel: with-wall-or-hedge enclose (Num 32:16,24,36, Job 19:8, Ps 89:41, Prov 24:31, Hos 2:8, Amos 9:11, Mic 7:11). Hyphenated.
Proper noun, Canaanite place; Josh 12:13; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Geder.
Town-name from Judah's lowland (Josh 12:13; 15:36; 1Chr 4:18; 12:5; 27:28; 1Kgs 4:10). English convention: Geder.
Low dry-built stone-fence for-vineyard or-pasture-field distinguished from chomah (city-wall, H2346) by agricultural-border-aspect (Num 22:24, Ps 62:4, 80:13, Prov 24:31, Eze 13:5, 22:30, 42:7,10).
Female form of gader (stone-wall) with specifically-functional meaning as-sheep-pen-stall (Num 32:16,24,36, 1Sam 24:4, Zeph 2:6).
Proper noun, Judah-city lowland; Josh 15:36; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gederah.
Gentilic from Gedera (1Chr 27:28 Baal-Hanan-David's-officer); from H1445 Gedera-city.
Proper noun, Judah-city lowland; Josh 15:36; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gederothaim.
Elijah-bow-down-pray-Carmel and Elisha-stretch-himself-on-dead-child (1Kgs 18:42; 2Kgs 4:34,35). Hyphenated to distinguish bow-down-stoop-crouch-aspect from H7812 shachah 'bow-down-worship'.
YHWH-behind-back-cast and psalm-behind-back-law-cast and sinner-Job's-back (1Kgs 14:9; Neh 9:26; Isa 38:17). Hyphenated.
Aramaic form for 'inside/midst'; furnace-midst (Dan 3:6,11,15,21,23-26), lions'-den-midst (Dan 6:7,12,16-17,24), visions 'in the midst of the night' (Dan 7:15).
Back- or body-middle as target of strokes (Prov 10:13; 19:29; 26:3; Isa 38:17; 50:6). Hyphenated to distinguish back-side-aspect from homonym H1460b gev-II 'inside'.
Hapax Job 30:5 body-people-driven-out; sub-sense pair with H1460a back same root.
Locust as plague-creature - in Amos 7:1 (the former of locusts in the beginning of the late-growth) and Nahum 3:17 (your princes are as locusts); distinguished from H1462a gov-I (great-heap).

Reubenite (1Chr 5:4) and apocalyptic-enemy in eschatological-prophecy - Eze 38:2,3,14,16,18, 39:1,11,15 'set your-face against Gog of-land-Magog prince-of-Rosh-Meshech-Tubal' - future-great-onslaught.
Raiding-bands against Gad-wordplay (Gen 49:19 three times). Hyphenated to distinguish raid-press-overcome-aspect from H6555 parats 'break-through' (already assigned).

Original concordant: pride-haughtiness-self-exaltation. Lowly-bowed-deliver-by-pride-laying-down and Job-man-from-his-pride-laying-aside and Jer-heart-pride-disciplined (Job 22:29; 33:17; Jer 13:17). Hyphenated.
Aramaic parallel to gaavah; in-pride-walking humble; Dan 4:37.
Num-wind-brought-quail-from-sea and Ps-you-have-passed-his-life-quickly (Num 11:31; Ps 90:10). Hyphenated to distinguish sweep-bring-pass-over-aspect from H1494 gazaz 'shear'.
River and region to which Israel was deported (2Kgs 17:6; 18:11; 19:12; 1Chr 5:26; Isa 37:12). English convention: Gozan.

Root gwh. Political-territorial entity. To be distinguished from am (H5971a, people as common-descent). 'Nation' preserves that distinction; 'gentile/heathen' is a later cultural choice that breaks concordance.
Original concordant: Goyim-peoples-coalition-Tidal-kingdom. Gen-Tidal-king-Goyim and Gen-same-coalition-Tidal-Goyim and Josh-king-Goyim-of-Gilgal-one (Gen 14:1,9; Josh 12:23). Hyphenated.
Body (living or as corpse), fig. mummy; the hyphenated English marks dead or unanimated dimension.
From √galah (carry-away); both the state and the group of exiles; concordantly 'exile'.
Bashanite city-of-refuge for manslayers (Deut 4:43; Josh 20:8; 21:27; 1Chr 6:71). English convention: Golan.
Hapax Eccl 10:8 digger-pit-falls-in; possibly loan of uncertain origin.
Naphtali-son and Gad-family (Gen 46:24; Num 26:48; 1Chr 5:15; 7:13). English convention: Guni. 'Protected'.
Patronym-clan son of Naphtali; Num 26:48; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gunite.
Qal: undergo death-struggle, expire; the hyphenated English marks the moment of life-end.
Hiphil; Jerusalem-gates bolted on time; Neh 7:3.
Root gwr. Temporarily dwell as stranger. 'Sojourn' preserves the temporary stranger-status; derived ger (H1616).
Throng-together in fear or against someone (Ps 56:7; 59:4; Isa 54:15; Hos 7:14). Hyphenated; distinguishes group-gathering from homonym H1481a gur 'sojourn'.
Third homonym distinguished from gur-I (sojourn, H1481a) and gur-II (raise-strife, H1481b); Qal: anxiously-shrink-back-from (Num 22:3, Deut 1:17, 18:22, 32:27, Ps 22:24, 33:8).
Lion-or jackal-whelp (Gen 49:9; Deut 33:22; Jer 51:38; Eze 19:2,3,5; Lam 4:3; Nah 2:13). Hyphenated to mark suckling-young; distinguished from homonyms H1481a 'sojourn' and H1481b 'band-together'.
Proper noun, place where Ahaziah was wounded; 2Kgs 9:27; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gur.
Proper noun, place of Arabs whom Uzziah defeated; 2Chr 26:7; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gur-Baal.
Unique lexeme. Dice-event, allotted portion. 'Lot' covers both the means and the outcome.
The earth-clods under which Job's skin is swollen - Job 7:5 (my skin is broken and become loathsome) and figuratively the bodies of the dying who return to dust.
Original concordant: fleece-shearing-mowing-shorn-quantity. Wool-shearing-firstfruits-priest and king-shearing and Gideon-fleece and king-mowing-portion (Deut 18:4; Amos 7:1; Ps 72:6). Hyphenated.
Aramaic parallel to Hebrew gizbar; Persian empire-financiers; Ezra 7:21.
Wool of sheep snip-off as annual harvest-feast (Gen 31:19; 38:12,13; Deut 15:19; 1Sam 25:2,4,7,11; 2Sam 13:23,24; Job 1:20; Isa 53:7; Jer 7:29; Mic 1:16). Hyphenated.
Patronym-clan David's-warrior Hashem; 1Chr 11:34; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gizonite.
Qal: clip wool of sheep, cut head-hair; concordantly 'shear'.
Stone-with-smooth-hewn-surface by-skilled-stonemason distinguished from eben (rough-stone, H68) by working-aspect (Ex 20:25 = Deut 27:5 altar-prohibition).
Qal: take by force; distinguished from ganav (steal); concordantly 'rob'.

Violently-taken goods or oppression (Lev 5:21; Ps 62:11; Eccl 5:7; Isa 61:8). Hyphenated to distinguish the plunder-spoil-aspect from H7998 shalal 'spoil' and H961 bizzah 'plunder' (already assigned).
Wrongfully-taken goods (Lev 5:23; Eze 18:7,12,16; 33:15; Isa 61:8; Prov 4:17). Hyphenated to preserve plunder-result; family with H1497 gazal 'rob-seize'.

Original concordant: shearer-locust-bare-eater-species. Joel-what-the-shearer-locust-left-the-locust-ate and Amos-as-king-your-fig-trees-shearer-locust-devoured and Joel-years-which-shearer-locust-ate (Joel 1:4; 2:25; Amos 4:9). Hyphenated.
Head of a Nethinim-family in the return-list - Ezra 2:48, Nehemiah 7:51.
Job-cut-off-tree-stump-can-sprout-again and Isaiah-Jesse-stump-shoot-Messiah and God-plants-barely-stump (Job 14:8; Isa 11:1; 40:24). Hyphenated.
Qal/Niphal: cleave in two (child, sea, cut-covenant 'cut'), cut off; concordantly 'cut-through'.

Original concordant: decree-cut-determine-aramaic. Aramaic-decree hew-out and stone-hewn-without-hands (Dan 2:34,45; 4:14,24; 7:26). Hyphenated to distinguish decree-cut-aramaic-aspect from H1504 gazar 'cut-off-cut' and H2852 chathakh.
Original concordant: covenant-piece-sacrifice-portion-cut-asunder. Gen-flame-of-fire-passed-between-the-pieces and Ps-who-divided-the-Red-Sea-into-parts (Gen 15:17; Ps 136:13). Hyphenated.
Proper noun; Canaanite city on Philistine border, Levitical city; concordantly transliterated.
External-body-shape or set-apart-place (Lam 4:7; Eze 41:12,13,14,15; 42:1,10,13). Hyphenated to distinguish form-cut-aspect from H8403 tavnith 'pattern' and H6697 tsur 'rock'.
Uninhabited region where scapegoat goes; Lev 16:22.
Aramaic word for decree or decision - in Daniel 4:17 (the matter is in the decree of the watchers) and Daniel 4:24 (this is the interpretation, and this is the decree); heavenly council-decree.
Burning charcoal-piece for fire and incense-burning; the hyphenated English marks state.
Proper noun, son of Nahor; Gen 22:24; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gaham.
Head of a Nethinim-family in the return-list - Ezra 2:47, Nehemiah 7:49.
Narrow incised valley; distinguished from emek (lowland) and nachal (stream-valley); the hyphenated English marks incision.
Hip-sinew/tendon, occasion for Israel's food-law (Gen 32:33; Job 10:11; 40:17; Isa 48:4; Eze 37:6,8). Hyphenated; anatomical connecting-tissue between bone and flesh.
Water or fruit out-burst (Judg 20:33; Job 38:8; 40:23; Ps 22:10; Eze 32:2; Mic 4:10). Hyphenated to preserve breakthrough-eruption.
Proper noun, place near Ammah-hill; 2Sam 2:24; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Giah.
Eden-river and water-spring at Jerusalem (Gen 2:13; 1Kgs 1:33,38,45; 2Chr 32:30; 33:14). English convention: Gihon.
Servant of prophet Elisha during Shunammite-narrative (2Kgs 4:12-14,25,27,29-32,36 intermediary at son-promise-and-resurrection), at-healing-of-Naaman commits-greedy-deceit and-becomes-leprous.
Qal: noisily rejoice; often in parallel with samach; concordantly 'rejoice-loudly'.
Exuberant joy-manifestation of people or harvest (Ps 43:4; 45:16; 65:13; Isa 16:10; Joel 1:16; Hos 9:1). Hyphenated to distinguish expression-joy-aspect from H8057 simchah 'joy-state'.
Inhabitant of Giloh; Ahithophel's-epithet; 2Sam 15:12; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gilonite.
Aramaic for plaster-wall on which hand-wrote; Dan 5:5.
Proper noun, son of Jahdai-Caleb-branch; 1Chr 2:47; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Geshan.
From √galal (roll); rolled-stone-heap as memorial or ruin; concordantly 'heap-of-stones'.
Mountain-ridge in the north; scene of Saul's death (1Sam 28:4; 31:1,8; 2Sam 1:6,21; 21:12; 1Chr 10:1,8). English convention: Gilboa.
Reduplicated-form of √galal (roll, H1556); whirling-wheel distinguished from ofan (wheel, H212) by whirlwind-or-wind-whirl-aspect (Ps 77:19, 83:14, Isa 17:13, Eze 10:2,6,13).
Proper noun ('circle/wheel'); first encampment after Jordan-crossing; concordantly transliterated.
From √galal (roll); cranium, per-capita-counting ('per head'), place Golgotha 'place-of-the-skull'; concordantly 'skull'.
Job sews sackcloth on his skin; Job 16:15.
Root glh. Make uncovered, reveal, lead into exile (uncovering of land). 'Uncover' preserves the kernel-uncovering-action across all fields.

Original concordant: reveal-lead-into-exile-aramaic. Aramaic cognate of H1540 galah with double-meaning: reveal (Dan 2:19,22,28-30,47) and lead-into-exile (Ezra 4:10, 5:12); Aramaic context of Ezra-Daniel uses both aspects.
Round-bowl on lampstand or pillar (2Chr 4:12,13; 1Kgs 7:41,42; Zech 4:2,3; Eccl 12:6). Hyphenated to distinguish bowl-globe-aspect from H4219 mizraq 'sprinkling-bowl' and H3713 kefor 'basin'.
Pejorative term for idol-images, root √galal (roll/dung); the hyphenated English preserves the contemptuous load.
Wrap-mantles of blue and embroidered; Eze 27:24.
From √galah (uncover, carry-away); deportation into captivity (Babylon); concordantly 'exile'.
Zerubbabel-with-return-from-exile and Daniel-with-deported-of-Judah (Ezra 6:16; Dan 2:25; 5:13; 6:14). Hyphenated to distinguish exile-deportees-aramaic-aspect from Hebrew galut.
Piel: shave off hair (nazirite, leper, priest); concordantly 'shave'.
Mirror or polishing wax-tablet - in Isaiah 3:23 (the mirrors and the fine linen and the hoods) and Isaiah 8:1 (take a great roll and write on it with a man's pen); shining-polished surface.

Original concordant: district-circle-region-Galilee. District or circle-region (especially 'district of the gentiles' > later Galilee) - in Isaiah 8:23 (the district of the gentiles, Galil ha-goyim) and Joel 3:4 (all you districts of Palestina); extension of H1550a.
Northern hill-region of Israel (Josh 20:7; 21:32; 1Kgs 9:11; 2Kgs 15:29; 1Chr 6:76; Isa 8:23). English convention: Galilee.
Border-district or surrounding region (Josh 13:2; 18:17; 22:10,11; Eze 47:8; Joel 3:4). Hyphenated to preserve district-encircled-aspect; family with H1556 galal.
Proper noun ('circuits') Benjamin-border-place; Josh 18:17; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Geliloth.
Philistine giant defeated by David (1Sam 17:4,23; 21:10; 22:10; 2Sam 21:19; 1Chr 20:5). English convention: Goliath.
From √galal (roll, H1556); 'on-grounds-of' as prepositional-dependent-object, always in 'bi-galal' = 'because-of' (Gen 12:13, 30:27, 39:5).
Galal-Levite-temple-singer-post-exile-Jerusalem and Galal-twice-in-Levite-registers (1Chr 9:15,16; Neh 11:17). English convention: Galal. 'Rolled-roller' or 'beneficent' (family with galal-roll).
Large hewn block-stones with which the walls of the second temple were built - Ezra 5:8, 6:4; Aramaic, related to rolling-turning because of size.
Image of transience and humiliation (Job 20:7; 1Kgs 14:10; Zeph 1:17; Eze 4:12,15). Hyphenated to distinguish dung-refuse-aspect from H1828 domen 'dung-heap' (already assigned) and H6569 peresh.
Proper noun, Levi-singer wall-dedication-procession; Neh 12:36; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gilalai.
Qal; Elijah folded his mantle to strike Jordan; 2Kgs 2:8.
Your-eyes saw my-unformed-substance; Ps 139:16. NL refined audit-2026-04-26: root g-l-m fold-roll; embryo was modern medical import.
Original concordant: lonely-barren-childless-forsaken. Job-barren-not-bearing and Isa-you-were-childless-forsaken and Ps-barren-lonely (Job 3:7; 15:34; 30:3; Isa 49:21). Hyphenated.
Prov-before-fool-breaks-out-strife and Prov-wise-restrains-sudden-anger and Prov-strife-breaks-through-as-water (Prov 17:14; 18:1; 20:3). Hyphenated.
Ethnonym-adjective of Gilead (H1568) for inhabitant or descendant; Jephthah's origin (Judg 10:3 Jair, 11:1,40, 12:4,5,7), Barzillai's loyalty (2Sam 17:27, 19:32, 1Kgs 2:7).

Cascade or flow down as hair from a mountain-side - in Song of Songs 4:1 (your hair is as a flock of goats descending from mount Gilead) and Song 6:5 (your hair is as a flock of goats appearing from Gilead).
Additive particle. 'Also' covers the additive function.
Nile-papyrus for basket-weaving (Ex 2:3; Job 8:11; Isa 18:2; 35:7). Hyphenated to distinguish papyrus-rush-aspect from H7070 qaneh 'reed' and H100 agmon 'rush-reed' (already assigned).
Short measure (about a cubit) Ehud-sword; Judg 3:16.
Proper noun, watcher-people on Tyre-towers; Eze 27:11; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gammadite.
From √gamal (recompense); deserved reward or punishment; concordantly 'recompense'.
Proper noun, twenty-second priest-lot David's-time; 1Chr 24:17; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gamul.
Barzillai-David-recompense-decline and peoples-vengeance-recompense (2Sam 19:37; Isa 59:18; Jer 51:56; Ps 94:2). Hyphenated to distinguish recompense-reward-aspect from H1576 gemul.
Proper noun, place taken by Philistines under Ahaz; 2Chr 28:18; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gimzo.
Qal: pay back (good or evil), bring to maturity; concordantly 'recompense'.
Proper noun, father of Ammiel-spy of Dan; Num 13:12; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gemalli.
Manassite tribe-head at Sinai-numbering (Num 1:10; 2:20; 7:54,59; 10:23). English convention: Gamaliel. 'Recompense-of-God'.

Original concordant: complete-perfect-bring-to-end. God complete-perfect for righteous (Ps 7:10; 12:2; 57:3; 138:8). Hyphenated to distinguish complete-perfect-aspect from H3615 kalah 'finish' (already assigned) and H8552 tamam 'finish'.
People-son of Japheth and Hosea's wife (Gen 10:2,3; 1Chr 1:5,6; Eze 38:6; Hos 1:3). English convention: Gomer.
Two pious men in Jeremiah's time (Jer 29:3; 36:10,11,12,25). English convention: Gemariah. 'YHWH-has-completed'.
Enclosed garden; cultural-space against wilderness; concordantly 'garden'.
Qal: secretly take away; distinguished from gazal (violently rob); concordantly 'steal'.
Ex-found-living-in-his-hand-the-theft and Ex-shall-restore-double (Ex 22:2,3). Hyphenated to distinguish theft-stolen-goods-aspect from H1589 ganav 'steal' (already assigned).

Original concordant: Genubath-son-Hadad-Edom-Egypt. 1K-the-sister-of-Tahpenes-bore-him-his-son-Genubath and 1K-Genubath-was-in-the-house-of-Pharaoh-among-the-sons-of-Pharaoh (1K 11:20 cf; 11:20). Hyphenated.
Female parallel-form of gan (garden, H1588); planted-enclosed-garden with specific-ornamental-plants distinguished from common-garden (Isa 1:29-30, 65:3, 66:17; Song 6:11).
Tibni's father at Israel-division and Levite family-head (1Kgs 16:21,22; Neh 12:4,16). English convention: Ginnath. 'Garden-grove'.

Original concordant: treasure-chest-royal-treasure-storage. Esther's-royal-treasure and Mordecai-crown-property-Persian-royal-treasury and Eze-precious-chests-of-trade-goods (Esth 3:9; 4:7; Eze 27:24). Hyphenated.

Original concordant: treasury-storehouse-royal-aramaic. King-decree-search-in-treasury and royal-treasury-of-Babel (Ezra 5:17; 6:1; 7:20). Hyphenated to distinguish treasury-storehouse-royal-treasure-aramaic-aspect from Hebrew genez.

As protective-shield over something-or-someone stand (2Kgs 19:34; 20:6; Isa 31:5; 37:35; 38:6; Zech 9:15; 12:8). Hyphenated; distinguishes protect-roof-action from H1588 gan 'garden' (enclosed space).
Ginnethon-priestly-family-returnee-Zerubbabel and Ginnethon-sealer-covenant-renewal-Nehemiah (Neh 10:7; 12:4,16). English convention: Ginnethon. 'Garden-like-garden-hortus' (family with H1588 gan).
Proper noun, border-place Jerusalem-extension; Jer 31:39; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Goah.
Inwardly turn-away from someone or something; God of his people (Lev 26:11,15,30,43,44; Eze 16:45). Hyphenated to preserve deep-aversion-reaction; distinguishes from H8581 ta'av and homonym H1351.
Ephraimite rebel son-of-Eved - led-revolt against-Abimelech (Judg 9:26-41 core-account); concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gaal.
Qal: authoritatively reprimand, threaten (YHWH rebukes the sea, Satan); concordantly 'rebuke'.
From √gaar (rebuke); angry forbidding-utterance (YHWH rebukes waves, enemies); the hyphenated English marks voice-elevation.
Quaking of earth or commotion of sea (2Sam 22:8; Ps 18:8; Jer 5:22; 25:16; 46:7,8; Job 34:20). Hyphenated to preserve commotion-surge.
Gaash-mountain where Joshua-buried-is and David's-warrior (Josh 24:30; Judg 2:9; 2Sam 23:30; 1Chr 11:32). English convention: Gaash. 'Quaking' or 'shaking' (family with ga'ash-shake-tremble).
Own-person as independent unit (Ex 21:3,4; Job 20:22; Prov 9:3; 1Kgs 14:5). Hyphenated to distinguish alone-self-aspect from H905 bad 'alone' and H909 badad 'separately'.
Dan-aramaic-lion-had-eagle's-wings and Dan-aramaic-wings-plucked-out and Dan-aramaic-four-wings-of-bird (Dan 7:4 twice, 7:6). Hyphenated to distinguish wing-aramaic-aspect from H3671 kanaf-Hebrew.
Combustible sulphur-stone, instrument of judgment (Gen 19:24; Deut 29:22; Job 18:15; Ps 11:6; Isa 30:33; 34:9; Eze 38:22). Natural mineral; concordantly preserved untranslated.
Root gwr (sojourn-as-stranger, H1481a). 'Sojourner' preserves the non-native status.
Benjamite family-name; connected to Ehud and Shimei (Gen 46:21; Judg 3:15; 2Sam 16:5; 19:16,18; 1Kgs 2:8; 1Chr 8:3,5,7). English convention: Gera.
Unclean-scabby-skin-disease for offering-disqualifying and judgment-scab-plague (Lev 21:20; 22:22; Deut 28:27). Hyphenated to distinguish scab-itch-skin-disease-aspect from H7822 shechin.
Gareb-Ithrite-one-of-David's-thirty and hill-Gareb-near-Jerusalem (2Sam 23:38; 1Chr 11:40; Jer 31:39). English convention: Gareb. 'Leprous-scratch' or 'scab-spot' (family with H1618 garav).

Original concordant: throat-neck-gullet-neck-part. Throat-place for words and neck-ornament (Prov 1:9; 3:3,22; 6:21). Hyphenated to distinguish throat-neck-gullet-aspect from H1627 garon 'throat-gullet' (already assigned) and H6677 tsavvar 'neck'.
One of the seven Canaanite peoples (Gen 10:16; 15:21; Deut 7:1; Josh 3:10; 24:11; 1Chr 1:14; Neh 9:8). English convention: Girgashite.
Hithpael; Job scraped himself with potsherd on ash; Job 2:8.
Hithpael: meddle in strife, provoke (seek war); the hyphenated English marks confrontation.
Lump-of-food which ruminants from fore-stomach bring-back-up; only in idiom 'bring-up-of-gerah' = chew-cud as clean-animal-mark (Lev 11:3-7,26 camel-hare-coney-pig-classification, Deut 14:6-8).
Smallest silver-weight-unit twentieth-of-shekel (Ex 30:13; Lev 27:25; Num 3:47; 18:16; Eze 45:12). Hyphenated to preserve smallest-weighing-unit.

Throat-organ as source of voice or swallow-passage (Ps 5:10; 69:4; 115:7; 149:6; Prov 3:3; Isa 3:16; 58:1; Jer 2:25; Eze 16:11). Hyphenated to preserve anatomical precision (no H3956 lashon 'tongue').
People-rested in temporary-sojourn near Bethlehem; Jer 41:17.
Blessing-mountain opposite Ebal in Samaria (Deut 11:29; 27:12; Josh 8:33; Judg 9:7). English convention: Gerizim. 'Hewn-mountain-pieces'.
Wood-axe for tree-felling or building-tool (Deut 19:5 twice; 20:19; 1Kgs 6:7; Isa 10:15). Hyphenated to distinguish axe-cutting-iron-aspect from H4621 ma'atsad 'hand-axe' and H7049 qela.
Num-gnaw-bones-Moab and Eze-men-of-war-daughter-of-judge-his-bones-gnaw (Num 24:8; Eze 23:34). Hyphenated to distinguish break-gnaw-bones-aspect from H1633a garam.
Bone-skeleton of body or object (Gen 49:14; 2Kgs 9:13; Job 40:18; Ps 53:6; Prov 17:22; 25:15). Hyphenated to distinguish bone-skeleton-aspect from H1472 geviyah 'corpse-body' and H6106 etsem.
Patronym-clan Keilah-Judah-branch; 1Chr 4:19; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Garmite.
Flat open place where grain is threshed and winnowed; concordantly 'threshing-floor'.

The crushing or grinding - Psalm 119:20 (my soul breaks for the longing it has unto Your judgments at all times) and Lamentations 3:16 (He has also broken my teeth with gravel-stones, He has covered me with ashes).
Qal: take away, withhold, shorten; concordantly 'diminish'.
Chewing the cud as clean-mark of animal (Lev 11:7; Deut 14:7,8; 1Kgs 14:11; Hab 1:15). Hyphenated to distinguish chew-cud-aspect from homonym H1641a garar-I 'drag' and H4573 ma'ar.

Philistine city-state southwest of Israel under king Abimelech; Abraham's temporary-residence (Gen 20:1-2,18 Sarah-as-sister), Isaac's-well-controversies (Gen 26:1-26 well-repetition, blessing-strife), Asa's victory.
What the sun drives forth out of the earth; Deut 33:14.
Firstborn son of Moses by Zipporah (Ex 2:22, 18:3); 'sojourner-there'; Levitical main-line (1Chr 6:16-17, 23:15-16, 26:24); also Ezra-contemporary (Ezra 8:2); concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun ('exiled-one'); eldest son of Levi; concordantly transliterated.
Patronymic 'Gershonites'; Levitical-clan of Gershon (Num 3, 4, 26, 1Chr 6); concordantly transliterated.
Aramean-kingdom east-of-Sea-of-Galilee - father-in-law-territory of-David (Deut 3:14, 2Sam 3:3 Maacah-mother-of-Absalom, 13:37-38, 14:23,32, 15:8). English convention: Geshur.
Gentilic of Geshur, Aramean neighbour-people (Deut 3:14; Josh 12:5; 13:2,11,13; 1Sam 27:8). English convention: Geshurite.
Hapax Jer 14:22 heavens-give-rain; from H1653 geshem rain.
Heavy rainfall, in dry season malign; distinguished from matar (ordinary rain); concordantly 'downpour'.
Arabian-opponent of Nehemiah at wall-rebuilding (Neh 2:19; 6:1,2,6). English convention: Geshem. Distinguished from homonym H1653 geshem 'rain' (already assigned).
Aramaic-equivalent for fleshly-body in Daniel (Dan 3:27,28; 4:30; 5:21; 7:11). Hyphenated to mark Aramaic-parallel; distinguished from Hebrew H1653 geshem 'rain'.
Proper noun; eastern Nile-delta where Israel dwelt, and a city in Judah; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun, Nethinim-overseer alongside Ziha; Neh 11:21; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Gispa.
Press-vat in which grapes are trodden (Judg 6:11; Neh 13:15; Isa 63:2; Lam 1:15; Joel 3:13). Hyphenated to distinguish winepress-treading-aspect from H3342 yeqev 'winepress' and H6333 purah.
Proper noun ('winepress'); Philistine capital; concordantly transliterated.

Gentilic-inhabitant of-Gath - used-for Philistine-inhabitants and-for David's-elite-loyal-servants from-Gath (Josh 13:3, 2Sam 6:10-11 = 1Chr 13:13 Obed-Edom-the-Gittite, 2Sam 15:18-22 Ittai-the-Gittite).

Original concordant: Gittaim-Benjamin-city-two-presses. 2S-the-Beerothites-fled-to-Gittaim-and-have-been-sojourners-there and Neh-in-Hadid-Zeboim-Neballat-Lod-and-Ono-in-the-valley-of-craftsmen (2S 4:3; Neh 11:33). Hyphenated.
Psalms-title-designation (Ps 8:1, 81:1, 84:1); possibly from Gath-instrument H1661 or winepress.
Gen-sons-Aram-Uz-Hul-Gether-Mash and 1Chr-sons-Aram-Gether (Gen 10:23; 1Chr 1:17). Hyphenated to distinguish Gether-son-Aram-Aramean-tribe-aspect from other Aramean-eponyms; Semitic-tribe-eponym.
Aramaic-demonstrative in feminine form (Ezra 5:9; Dan 4:27; 5:6; 7:3,8). Hyphenated to mark feminine-parallel of H1836 denah 'this-aramaic' (masc.).
Ps-my-eyes-pine-from-tears and Jer-soul-faint-with-sorrow and Ps-die-with-soul-pining (Ps 88:10; Jer 31:12,25). Hyphenated to distinguish languish-pine-grieve-faint-aspect.
Inward concern or fear cherish about outcome (1Sam 9:5; 10:2; Ps 38:19; Isa 57:11; Jer 17:8; 38:19; 42:16). Hyphenated to distinguish anxiety-worry from H3025 yagor 'fear' (acute).
Edomite, chief-shepherd of Saul; Nob-slaughterer (1Sam 21:8; 22:9,18,22; Ps 52:2). English convention: Doeg.
Inward-worry that depresses the heart (Josh 22:24; Jer 49:23; Eze 4:16; 12:18,19; Prov 12:25). Hyphenated to distinguish brooding-fear-aspect from H6343 pachad 'fear' and H2731 charadah 'trembling'.
Bird-of-prey-swoop as speed-image (Deut 28:49; Jer 48:40; 49:22; Ps 18:11). Hyphenated to distinguish swoop-fly-aspect from H5774 uf 'fly' and H8582 ta'ah 'wander'; family with H1676.

Syrian-brown-bear as predator; David's lion-and-bear-experience (1Sam 17:34-37), comparison-courage (2Sam 17:8 'bear bereaved of cubs'), Elisha's two she-bears (2Kgs 2:24), wisdom-paradigm (Prov 17:12).
Hapax of uncertain core meaning; 'as-your-days-your-dove'; Deut 33:25.

Evil-slander-or-defaming-rumour distinguished from lashon-ra (evil-tongue) and rakil (slanderer) by rumour-character (Gen 37:2 Joseph 'brought their evil-report to-their-father', Num 13:32, 14:36-37, Ps 31:14, Prov 10:18, 25:10, Jer 20:10, Eze 36:3).
Wild-bee-swarm as war-image or destructive (Deut 1:44; Judg 14:8; Ps 118:12; Isa 7:18). Hyphenated to distinguish bee-swarm-aspect from homonym H1683 Deborah-person and H1706 devash 'honey'.
Rebekah's-nurse who was buried under 'Lament-oak' near Bethel (Gen 35:8); female-prophetess-judge who Sisera-defeat-orchestrated and triumph-song-sang (Judg 4:4,5,6,9,10,14, 5:1,7,12,15).
Aramaic Pael-participle; Jews offered in temple; Ezra 6:3.
Holy of holies in temple, innermost chamber; the hyphenated English marks position (distinguished from Debir pn).
Most-holy back chamber of temple (where Ark stood); the hyphenated English distinguishes from Devir II pn.
Second-sense Debir; Gad-border-place; Josh 13:26; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun ('fig-cake') north-border-destruction; Eze 6:14; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Diblah.
Pressed-dried-fig-disc as provision (1Sam 25:18; 30:12; 1Chr 12:41; Isa 38:21). Hyphenated to preserve pressed-fig-disc-aspect.
Father of Gomer-Hosea-wife (Hos 1:3); proper noun, plural-form fig-cake.
Qal: attach oneself to, follow; concordantly 'cleave' (also marriage-context Gen 2:24).
Aramaic cling-fast (Dan 2:43 not-cling-to-each-other); cognate Hebrew H1692 davaq.
Ahab-arrow-between-joints-of-armour and Isaiah-smith-soldering-joints (1Kgs 22:34; 2Chr 18:33; Isa 41:7). Hyphenated to distinguish joint-seam-cleaved-parts-aspect from H1695 daveq.

Original concordant: cleaving-clinging-loyal-attached. Adherents-clinging-to-YHWH and king-armour-clinging (Deut 4:4; 1Chr 10:6; 2Chr 3:12). Hyphenated to distinguish cleaving-clinging-loyal-aspect from H539 aman 'faithful'.
Root dbr. Piel-directed communication-activity. 'Speak' is the kernel-activity; davar (H1697) is the result.
Root dbr (speak, H1696). Davar is the spoken thing; encompasses 'matter' because matters in Hebrew are spoken-things.
Contagious deadly disease (plague); concordantly 'pestilence' (not 'plague' alone - broader).

Grassy pasture or grazing-area - in Isaiah 5:17 (the lambs shall feed after their manner, and the strangers shall eat the waste places of the fat ones) and Micah 2:12 (I will surely assemble them as the sheep of Bozrah).
The matter or cause concerning which something is spoken - Psalm 110:4 (you are a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek), Eccl 3:18, 7:14, 8:2, Job 5:8; variant-form of H1697 davar.
Proper noun, Danite-father of Shelomith; Lev 24:11; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Dibri.
Daberath-city in Issachar-Zebulon-border and Levite-city (Josh 19:12; 21:28; 1Chr 6:57). English convention: Daberath. 'Pasture-place' (family with H1699 dover-pasture).
Honey from bees and grape-syrup; concordantly 'honey'.
Treasures on camel-humps to Egypt; Isa 30:6.
Proper noun, Zebulon-border-place; Josh 19:11; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Dabbesheth.
Scaly sea-creature, created on day 5; concordantly 'fish'.
Collective: fish as species (more than just animal); the hyphenated English distinguishes from dag 'fish'.
Proper noun; Philistine deity (fish/grain-god), temple in Gaza/Ashdod; concordantly transliterated.
Army-banner of a tribe in wilderness-camp (Num 2); the hyphenated English marks function.
General term for grain (wheat, barley); concordantly 'corn' (distinguished from chittah wheat).
Brood or hatch eggs - in Isaiah 34:15 (there shall the wild owl make her nest and lay and hatch) and Jeremiah 17:11 (as the partridge gathers eggs which she has not laid).
Suckling-breast as love-image in Proverbs and prophets (Prov 5:19; Eze 23:3,8,21). Hyphenated to distinguish breast-suckling-aspect from H7699 shad 'mother-breast' (already assigned) and H2306 chad.
Walk solemnly or go slowly forward in procession - in Psalm 42:5 (I went with them solemnly to the house of God) and Isaiah 38:15 (I shall walk softly all my years for the bitterness of my soul).
Grandson of Cush (Gen 10:7, 1Chr 1:9) and son of Jokshan of Keturah (Gen 25:3, 1Chr 1:32); became Arabian trade-people associated with Tema (Jer 25:23, 49:8 'dwell deep', Eze 25:13 'from Teman').
Second-sense Dedan; Edomite-trade-people Tyre; Eze 27:15; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun, Arabian caravans lodging in thickets; Isa 21:13; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Dedanites.
Aramaic noun: gold; parallel to Hebrew zahav; concordantly compound with language-marker.
Aramaic gentilic exiles-people (Ezra 4:9); identity uncertain, possibly Daha-tribe.

Original concordant: galloping-stamping-horse-hooves. Judg-then-the-horse-hooves-stamped-by-the-galloping-the-galloping-of-their-mighty-ones and Nah-the-leaping-of-horses-and-the-jumping-of-chariots (Judg 5:22; Nah 3:2 cf). Hyphenated.
Fisher or catcher - in Ezekiel 47:10 (the fishers shall stand upon it) and Jeremiah 16:16 (I will send for many fishers, says the LORD, and they shall fish them); near-variant of H1770 dug.
Beloved person (uncle, lover, beloved); in Song of Songs the beloved; concordantly 'beloved'.
Large ceramic cooking-pot or basket (1Sam 2:14; 2Chr 35:13; Job 41:12; Ps 81:7; Jer 24:1,2). Hyphenated to mark food-preparation-vessel; distinguished from H5518 sir 'pot-kettle'.
Proper noun. Root dwd (love); meaning 'beloved'. Transliteration standard in English.

Original concordant: aunt-uncles-wife-related-female. Moses-aunt-Jochebed and uncle-sins-punishable (Ex 6:20; Lev 18:14; 20:20). Hyphenated to distinguish aunt-uncle's-wife-aspect from H5360 neqamah 'vengeance' and H1730a dod-I 'uncle-beloved'.
Three different persons: Issacharite judge and David's mighty men (Judg 10:1; 2Sam 23:9,24; 1Chr 11:12,26; 27:4). 'His-beloved'. English convention: Dodo.
Proper noun, father of prophet Eliezer; 2Chr 20:37; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Dodavahu.
Mandrake-plant-fruit with folk-belief-aphrodisiac (Gen 30:14,15,16; Song 7:14). Hyphenated to preserve amorous-folklore-load; no reduction to plant-name.
Proper noun, David's-army-commander second month; 1Chr 27:4; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Dodai.
Established-unclean by monthly flow or sickness (Lev 15:33; 20:18; Isa 30:22; Lam 1:13; 5:17). Hyphenated to preserve female-cycle-uncleanness-aspect; family with H1738 davah.
Ritual-filth wash-off or soul-purification (2Chr 4:6; Isa 4:4; Jer 51:34; Eze 40:38). Hyphenated to distinguish cleansing-rinse-aspect from H7857 shataf 'overflow' and H3526 kavas 'wash'.
The exhausting bodily misery - Job 6:7 (my soul refuses to touch what is to me as sorrowful meat) and Psalm 41:4 (on the bed of languishing); from H1738 davah (menstruate-be-sick).
Lam-sick-weakening-heart and Isa-sick-heart and Isa-no-more-sick-shall-I-be-faint (Lam 1:22; 5:17; Isa 1:5; Jer 8:18). Hyphenated to distinguish languishing-weak-aspect.
Lev-stork-heron-hoopoe-bat and Deut-heron-hoopoe-bat (Lev 11:19; Deut 14:18). Hyphenated to distinguish hoopoe-cuckoo-unclean-aspect from other birds.

Original concordant: silence-stillness-death-silence. The silence of the realm of the dead where God is not praised - Psalm 94:17 (my soul had almost dwelt in silence) and Psalm 115:17 (the dead praise not the LORD, neither any that go down into silence).
Edomite descendant and Arabian region (Gen 25:14; 1Chr 1:30; Josh 15:52; Isa 21:11). English convention: Dumah. 'Silence-stillness'.

The waiting silence before God - Psalm 22:3 (in the night seasons and am not silent), 39:3 (I was dumb with silence), 62:2 (truly my soul waits silently for God) and 65:2 (praise waits for You, O God in Zion).
Isa-they-sit-silently-on-the-ground and Lam-let-him-sit-alone-in-silence and Hab-awaken-stone-in-silence (Isa 47:5; Lam 3:26; Hab 2:19). Hyphenated to distinguish silent-quietly-soundless-aspect.
Melting-wax as image of enemies before God (Ps 22:15; 68:3; 97:5; Mic 1:4). Hyphenated to distinguish wax-beeswax-aspect from H4549 masas 'melt' (already assigned) and H5413 nathakh 'pour-out'.
Qal-infinitive; David prefers temple-doorpost over wicked-tents; Ps 84:10.
Aramaic Peal: inhabit/dwell as permanent dwelling-place (Dan 2:38, 3:31, 4:9,18,32,35, 5:19, 6:25). Concordantly via '-aramaic'.
Ball or globe-shaped object - in Isaiah 22:18 (He will surely roll you as a ball) and Isaiah 29:3 (I will encamp against you in a circle); concrete-geometric form, related to dur (go around).
Second-sense dur; Shebna-as-ball-hurled into wide land; Isa 22:18.
Unique lexeme. Generation as time-unit and as group of people. 'Generation' covers both under one word.
Phoenician coastal city at Carmel-foot (Josh 11:2; 12:23; 17:11; Judg 1:27; 1Kgs 4:11; 1Chr 7:29). English convention: Dor.
Aramaic-proper-noun plain where Nebuchadnezzar-image stood; Dan 3:1; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Dura.
Qal: tread out grain or process with threshing-sledges, fig. crush enemy; concordantly 'thresh'.
Qal/Niphal/Pual: vigorous-push-down-or-overthrow distinguished from hadaph (push-away, H1920), nadach (drive-out, H5080), zanach (cast-off, H2186a), nagach (push-with-horns, H5055), and nagaph.
Second-sense dachah; false-prophets-slip in darkness; Jer 23:12.
Aramaic for diversion-entertainment for king not-brought-in; Dan 6:18.
Fall or stumbling - in Psalm 56:14 (that I may walk before God in the light of the living) and Psalm 116:8 (You have delivered my foot from falling); abstract from dacha (push, cause-to-fall).
Aramaic-verb for fear of God or king (Dan 2:31; 4:2; 5:19; 6:27; 7:7,19). Hyphenated to mark Aramaic-parallel; distinguished from Hebrew H2342 chul 'tremble'.
Hasty-pressing of royal-messenger and fleeing-people (2Chr 26:20; Esth 3:15; 6:12; 8:14). Hyphenated to distinguish urgent-driving-aspect from H5090a nahag 'drive-on'.
Measure-noun: what is sufficient, adequate amount; concordantly 'enough'.
Aramaic relative/genitive-marker, counterpart of asher (H834a). In Aramaic text-portions. 'Which' (with (A) marker in entry).
Moabite-Ammonite city east of Dead Sea, rebuilt by Gadites (Num 21:30, 32:3,34 Dibon-Gad, 33:45-46, Josh 13:9,17, Neh 11:25, Isa 15:2,9, Jer 48:18,22); concordantly transliterated.
Fisher as profession - in Isaiah 19:8 (also the fishers shall mourn) and Jeremiah 16:16 (I will send for many fishers, and they shall fish them); from H1770 dug (fish).
Proper noun ('enough-gold') place Moses-speech; Deut 1:1; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Di-zahab.

Original concordant: proper-name-Dimon-also-Dibon. Proper noun Dimon (variant of Dibon) - twice in one verse: Isaiah 15:9 (the waters of Dimon are full of blood, for I will bring more upon Dimon); wordplay with dam (blood) on place-name.
Proper noun, Judah-city south; Josh 15:22; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Dimonah.
Qal: settle a legal-case, judge; the hyphenated English marks the juridical action.

Original concordant: judge-render-decision-aramaic. The appointing of Aramaic judges who would judge the people - Ezra 7:25 (Ezra appoints judges and law-experts) and Daniel 7:10 (the judgment was set); Aramaic cognate of Hebrew din.
Aramaic-equivalent for legal-case or punishment (Ezra 7:26; Dan 4:34; 7:10,22,26). Hyphenated to mark Aramaic-parallel; family with H1779 din 'lawsuit' (Hebrew).
Daughter of Jacob and Leah; central figure in the Shechem-event (Gen 30:21; 34:1,3,5,13,25,26; 46:15). From din 'render-judgment'. As pn-nominal Dinah.
Surrounding-siege-wall around city (2Kgs 25:1; Jer 52:4; Eze 4:2; 17:17; 21:27; 26:8). Hyphenated to distinguish siege-rampart-aspect from H4692 matsor 'siege' and H5550 solelah 'earth-mound'.
Horite tribe-head among Seir's sons (Gen 36:21,25,26,30; 1Chr 1:38,41). English convention: Dishon; distinguished from H1789 Dishan.
Horite tribe-head among Seir's sons (Gen 36:21,28,30; 1Chr 1:38,42). English convention: Dishan; distinguished from H1787 Dishon.
Oppressed as YHWH-care-target (Ps 9:10; 10:18; 74:21; Prov 26:28). Hyphenated to distinguish oppressed-crushed-aspect from H6041 ani 'poor-afflicted' (already assigned) and H6035 anaw 'meek'.
Aramaic demonstrative pronoun (masculine singular) (Ezra 4:13,16,19,21; 5:17; 6:7,8; Dan 2:31; 4:15,27; 7:8,20,21). Linked via '-aramaic' to Hebrew demonstrative-family.
Piel: smash to dust, break in pieces; concordantly 'crush'.

The contrite spirit which God does not despise - Psalm 34:19 (the LORD is near to the broken-hearted and saves the contrite of spirit) and Isaiah 57:15 (I dwell with the contrite and the lowly of spirit).
Crushed-broken become of heart or bone (Ps 10:10; 44:20; 51:10; 51:19; Isa 19:10; 57:15). Hyphenated to distinguish inwardly-broken-aspect from H5310a natats-II 'shatter' and H4272 machats.

Original concordant: this-same-this-there-aramaic. Aramaic demonstrative pronoun for 'this/the-same' - in Daniel 2:18 (concerning this God of heaven) and Daniel 7:20 (and the horn that came up); demonstrative in Daniel's vision-context.
Ezra-sacrifice-temple-dedication-rams-with-lambs and rams-for-trespass-offering (Ezra 6:9,17; 7:17). Hyphenated to distinguish ram-male-sheep-offering-aramaic-aspect from Hebrew H2145 zakar 'male'.
Aramaic memorial-record-royal (Ezra 4:15, 6:2); from root dkr remember.
Socio-economically poor; distinguished from ani (oppressed) and evyon (needy-longing); concordantly 'needy'.
Height or wall leap-up like gazelle (2Sam 22:30; Isa 35:6; Zeph 1:9; Ps 18:30; Song 2:8). Hyphenated to distinguish leaping-stride-aspect from H5425 nathar 'leap-up'.
Water from well-up-pull or person-rescue (Ex 2:16,19; Ps 30:2; Prov 20:5; Isa 38:12). Hyphenated to distinguish well-up-pull-aspect from H5375 nasa 'lift' and H4899 mashach 'draw'.
The poor and lowly as remnant of the people - in 2Kings 24:14 (none remained but the poorest sort of the people of the land) and Jeremiah 40:7 (that he had committed unto him men, women, children).

Poor land-people who remained at exile (2Kgs 24:14; 25:12; Jer 40:7; 52:15,16). Hyphenated to distinguish socially-poor-people from homonym H1803a dallah-I 'thread-hair' (weave); family with H1800 dal.
Eze-with-feet-trouble-waters and Eze-troubled-streams and Eze-troubled-cattle-water (Eze 32:2,13; 34:18). Hyphenated to distinguish trouble-stir-up-muddy-aspect from H7515 rafas 'trample-water'.
Num-water-shall-flow-out-of-his-buckets and Isa-nations-as-drop-in-bucket (Num 24:7; Isa 40:15). Hyphenated to distinguish bucket-water-pail-aspect from H1809 dalal 'diminish'.
Various post-exilic persons (1Chr 3:24; 24:18; Ezra 2:60; Neh 6:10; 7:62; Jer 36:12,25). 'YHWH-has-drawn-up'. English convention: Delaiah.
Philistine woman who extracted Samson's secret (Judg 16:4,6,10,12,13,18). English convention: Delilah.
Hanging vine-branch or tree-branch (Jer 11:16; Eze 17:6,7,23; 19:11; 31:7,9,12). Hyphenated to preserve hanging-shoot-semantics (no H2156 zemorah 'pruning-branch').

Qal/Niphal: gradually-decline-to-powerlessness distinguished from rafah (slacken, H7503) and nafal (fall, H5307) by waste-from-high-to-low-aspect (Judg 6:6, Job 28:4, Ps 79:8, 116:6, 142:7, Isa 17:4, 19:6, 38:14).
Proper noun, Judah-city lowland; Josh 15:38; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Dilan.
The dripping of tears or of a leaking roof - Job 16:20 (to God my eye drips) and Proverbs 19:13 (the contentions of a wife are a continual dropping).

The continual dripping of a leaking roof as image of the contentious wife - Proverbs 19:13 (the contentions of a wife are a continual dropping) and Proverbs 27:15 (a continual dropping in a very rainy day).
Proper noun, second son of Haman; Esth 9:7; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Dalphon.
Qal/Hiphil: kindling-pursue distinguished from baar (burn, H1197a) and radaph (chase) by burning-pursuit-parallelism (Gen 31:36, Ps 7:14, 10:2, Prov 26:23, Obad 18).
Jer 36:23 scroll-pages-like-doors; sub-sense pair with H1817a door.
Qal: be like, resemble; Piel: imagine as; concordantly 'liken'.
Niphal/Qal: brought to silence, be destroyed; the hyphenated English distinguishes from damah I 'liken'.
Aramaic verb for being-like - in Daniel 3:25 (and the fourth is like the Son of God) and Daniel 7:5 (and it was like a bear); parallel of Hebrew damah.
From √damah (liken); abstract resemblance, image; concordantly 'likeness' (distinguished from tselem).
Ps-give-no-silence-to-yourself and Isa-silence-before-God-till-he-saves and Isa-watchmen-no-silence-cry (Ps 83:2; Isa 38:10; 62:6,7). Hyphenated.
Qal: become silent, come to silence (people, nature); concordantly 'be-still'.

Original concordant: silence-soft-whisper-stillness-calm. Elijah-soft-still-voice and Job's-soft-floating-stillness and psalm-storm-stillness (1Kgs 19:12; Job 4:16; Ps 107:29). Hyphenated to distinguish silence-soft-whisper-aspect from H8367 sheqet 'quietness'.
Animal-or-corpse-dung as pollution or fertiliser (2Kgs 9:37; Ps 83:11; Jer 8:2; 9:22; 16:4; 25:33). Hyphenated to preserve dung-manure-aspect.
Proper noun, Levi-city of Zebulon; Josh 21:35; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Dimnah.
Shed tears or weep - in Jeremiah 13:17 (my soul shall weep in secret places, and my eye shall weep sore) and Micah 2:6 (prophesy not, said the prophets to them).
Hapax-form; rest-couch on which Damascus-Israel sat; Amos 3:12.
Proper noun; capital of Aram/Syria; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun (son/tribe of Israel); concordantly transliterated.
Aramaic demonstrative pronoun: this; the hyphenated English marks language.
Proper noun, Judah-hill-country-city; Josh 15:49; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Dannah.
Designation of tribe-Dan (Judg 13:2; 18:1,11,30). Gentilic; family with H1835 Dan.
Variant attestation/spelling alongside H1841; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun, place David's-census-route; 2Sam 24:6; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Dan-jaan.
Religious-knowing or insight-knowledge (Job 32:6,10,17; 36:3; 37:16; Dan 12:4). Hyphenated to distinguish know-insight-aspect from H1847 da'ath 'knowledge' and H998 binah 'understanding'.
Mature-discernment of God or human (1Sam 2:3; Job 36:4; 37:16; Ps 73:11; Prov 24:14; Isa 11:9; 28:9; Jer 3:15). Hyphenated to distinguish ripened-insight-awareness from H1847 da'at.
Gadite tribe-prince and father of Eliasaph (Num 1:14; 7:42,47; 10:20). English convention: Deuel. 'God-knows'.
Extinguishing-going-out, often of lamp, fire or hope (Job 6:17; 17:1; 18:5,6; 21:17; Ps 118:12; Prov 13:9; 20:20; 24:20; Isa 43:17). Hyphenated; distinguishes passive-extinguished from H3518 kavah.
Root yd' (H3045). 'Knowledge' preserves the experiential knowing-kernel.
From √daqaq (pulverise); thin, fine-grained (manna 'fine as hoar-frost', lean cows); concordantly 'fine'.
Qal/Hiphil: shatter to dust (golden calf, idols), pulverise; the hyphenated English marks intensity.
Aramaic-cognate for breaking to dust (Dan 2:34,35,40,44,45; 7:7,19,23). Hyphenated to mark Aramaic-parallel; family with H1854 daqaq.

Qal/Niphal/Pual: with-pointed-weapon pierce/lance distinguished from naqav (pierce-with-hole, H5344a) (Num 25:8 Phinehas, Judg 9:54 Abimelech's-armour-bearer, 1Sam 31:4, 1Chr 10:4, Isa 13:15, Jer 37:10, 51:4, Lam 4:9, Zech 12:10, 13:3).
Aramaic-age of kingdom-without-end (Dan 3:33; 4:31,34; Ps 84:11). Hyphenated to distinguish generation-age-aramaic-aspect from H1755 dor 'generation' (already assigned); Aramaic cognate.

Original concordant: abhorrence-contempt-everlasting. Abhorrence or eternal contempt - in Daniel 12:2 (to everlasting abhorrence) and Isaiah 66:24 (they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh); eschatological term for judicial condemnation of the wicked.
Hapax Eccl 12:11 wise-words-as-ox-goads; sub-sense pair with H1861a goad.
Wise-man of Solomon-time 1Kgs 4:31 (compared with Solomon); son of Mahol-cluster.
South-direction of temple or land (Deut 33:23; Eze 40:24; 42:13; Eccl 1:6; 11:3). Hyphenated to distinguish south-noon-aspect from H5045 negev 'south-dry' and H3225 yamin 'right-hand-south'.
Great emancipation in jubilee-year, also 'swallow' as noun II; concordantly 'liberty'.
The free-flying bird (swallow-swift) as image of freedom - in Psalm 84:4 (the swallow has a nest where she lays her young) and Proverbs 26:2 (as the bird by wandering, as the swallow by flying).
Aramaic orthographic variant of Darius in Daniel-portions (Dan 6:1,2,7,10,13,26,29; 9:1; 11:1; Ezra 4:5; 5:5,6,7; 6:1,12,13,14,15; Hag 1:1,15; 2:10; Zech 1:1,7; 7:1). Concordantly via '-aramaic'.
Proper noun; Persian kings Darius the Mede and Darius I Hystaspes (Ezra, Dan); concordantly transliterated.
Qal: tread with foot (way, bend bow, tread wine); root of derech; concordantly 'tread'.
Root drk (tread, H1869). Beaten way, also metaphorically 'walk-of-life'. 'Way' covers both.
Darda-Mahol-son-wise-man-of-Solomon's-time and Darda-comparison-figure-wisdom-Solomon (1Kgs 5:11; 1Chr 2:6). English convention: Darda. 'Pearl-of-wisdom' or 'fore-knowledge' (dar-pearl).
Aramaic arm of image-silver (Dan 2:32); cognate Hebrew H2220 zeroa.
Proper noun, wise-man at Solomon-time; 1Chr 2:6; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Dara.
Head of a family of Solomon-servants in the return-list - Ezra 2:56, Nehemiah 7:58.
Root drsh. Investigate, seek answer. 'Inquire' preserves the seek-for-information dimension; 'seek' clashes with baqash (H1245).
Gen-earth-shall-fresh-green-bring-forth and Joel-pastures-wilderness-sprout and Isa-pastures-bring-forth-grassland (Gen 1:11; Joel 2:22; Isa 42:2). Hyphenated.
Fresh green plant-growth (day 3 of Creation); the hyphenated English marks freshness.
From deshen (fat-ash, H1880); Piel/Pual: with fat-oil-pour-over or satiate (Num 4:13 ash-removal of altar, Deut 31:20 Israel grow-fat, Ps 20:4 offering-favourably-receive, 23:5 head-with-oil-anoint).
Original concordant: well-fed-fat-rich-satiated-fruitful. Ps-well-fed-land and Isa-well-fed-with-fat-marrow and Deut-fat-and-well-fed-against-YHWH-kicks (Ps 22:30; 92:15; Isa 30:23). Hyphenated.
Fatty offering-ash of burnt-altar, fig. abundance; the hyphenated English marks composition.
Persian loanword; official edict of king, law; concordantly 'decree'.
Aramaic form of dat (decree, H1881); royal-edict/law (Ezra 7:12-14,21,25-26 'law of your Mighty-One and law of the king', Dan 2:9,13,15 decree-of-king, 6:5,8,12,15 'law of Medes and Persians', 7:25).

Original concordant: grass-field-green-pasture-aramaic. Aramaic word for grass-field or green pasture - in Daniel 4:15 (let his portion be with the beasts in the grass) and Daniel 4:23 (let his portion be with the beasts of the field); parallel of Hebrew deshe.
Aramaic loanword for law-expert or judge - in Daniel 3:2 (the judges) and Daniel 3:3 (the judges); Persian databara, judicial official in court-delegation.
Reubenite-son of Eliab who rebelled with Abiram and Korah against Moses-and-Aaron's-leadership and was-swallowed-by-the-earth (Num 16:1,12,24-25,27, 26:9, Deut 11:6, Ps 106:17).
Dothan-place-where-Joseph-sold and where-Elisha-Aramean-troops-sees (Gen 37:17 twice; 2Kgs 6:13). English convention: Dothan. 'Two-pits' or 'two-springs'.
Aramaic deictic-exclamation behold (Dan 2:43 divided-kingdom); alongside H1888a exclamation-other use.
Onomatopoeia of malicious-joy/triumph-cry (Ps 35:21,25, 40:16, 70:4, Job 39:25 war-horse snorts, Isa 44:16, Eze 25:3, 26:2, 36:2); concordantly 'Aha!' as English mocking-exclamation.
By empty-vanity be misled (2Kgs 17:15; Jer 2:5; 23:16; Job 27:12; Ps 62:11). Hyphenated to preserve vain-misleading-aspect; family with H1892 hevel 'vapour-vanity'.
Vapour, breath, fleetingness; key-word Ecclesiastes for transience; concordantly 'vapour-fleeting'. NL refined audit-2026-04-26: vapour-fleeting preserves root-metaphor h-b-l (vapour/breath).
Second son of Adam; shepherd-offerer killed by Cain (Gen 4:2,4,8,9,25; Job 16:18-analogue; Mat references via Heb OT-context). Homonym of H1892 hevel 'vanity'; proper-name reserved as Abel.

Chalk or tufa-limestone for wall-finishing - in Isaiah 27:9 (when He shall make all the stones of the altar as chalkstones beaten in pieces) and parallel-text; building-material-metaphor for altar-desecration.

Original concordant: divide-in-astrology-observe. Star-gazer verb for dividing the heaven into astrological sectors - in Isaiah 47:13 (let now the astrologers, the stargazers, the monthly prognosticators stand up).
Persian-eunuch-keeper of women's-court (Esth 2:3,8,15). English convention: Hegai. 'Pondering-meditation'.
Ps-take-away-the-wicked-from-king's-presence and Prov-take-away-grapes-and-gold and Isa-would-remove-the-wicked (Ps 115:6; Prov 25:4,5; Isa 27:8). Hyphenated.
Original concordant: muttering-murmur-thundering-sound-growl. Job-thundering-sound-God and Ps-my-meditation-thought-not-hidden and Lam-murmur-of-sighing (Job 37:2; Ps 90:9; Lam 3:62). Hyphenated.

Original concordant: meditation-murmur-string-music-quiet-meditation. Heart-meditation and harp-murmur as music-direction (Ps 9:17; 19:15; 92:4; Lam 3:62). Hyphenated to distinguish meditation-murmur-aspect from H7879 siach 'meditation' (already assigned).
Hapax Eze 42:12 temple-gates-protection; identity uncertain, possibly screen.
Proper noun; Egyptian slave of Sarai, mother of Ishmael; concordantly transliterated.
Descendants of Hagar, nomadic opponents (1Chr 5:10,19,20; 11:38; 27:31; Ps 83:7). English convention: Hagrite.
Aramaic-court-dignitary alongside satraps and governors (Dan 3:24,27; 4:33; 6:8). Hyphenated to distinguish counsellor-minister-courtier-aramaic-aspect from H3289 ya'ats 'counsel'.
Edomite king, son of Bedad (Gen 36:35-36, 1Chr 1:46); Hadad king of Edom contemporary of Solomon (1Kgs 11:14-25); concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun ('Hadad-is-help'); king of Zobah against David; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun, place where great-mourning-was; Zech 12:11; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Hadad-Rimmon.
India, the eastern-most province of Ahasuerus' empire of 127 provinces - Esther 1:1 (from Hoddu to Cush) and 8:9; derived from the Indus-river.
Hadoram-son-of-Joktan and Arabian-tribe-head (Gen 10:27; 1Chr 1:21). English convention: Hadoram. Distinguished from David's-envoy to king Tou H1913b Hadoram-II; 'Hadad-is-exalted'.
Second-sense Hadoram as personal-name tribute-master Rehoboam; 2Chr 10:18; concordantly transliterated.
Proper noun, David's-warrior from Naham-Gaash; 2Sam 23:30; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Hiddai.
Low-platform on which feet rest at throne (1Chr 28:2; Ps 99:5; 110:1; 132:7; Lam 2:1; Isa 66:1). Hyphenated to distinguish foot-platform from H134 eden 'socket-base' (base of pillar).
Fragrant myrtle for Feast of Tabernacles (Neh 8:15; Isa 41:19; 55:13; Zech 1:8,10,11). Hyphenated to mark myrtle-plant-specific.
Proper noun, Hebrew-name of Esther ('myrtle'); Esth 2:7; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Hadassah.

Qal: physical or figurative push-away/expel (Num 35:20,22 manslaughter by push, Deut 6:19 YHWH-thrusts-enemies-away, 9:4, Josh 23:5, 2Kgs 4:27 Shunammite not away, Job 18:18 'from-light-into-darkness-thrust', Prov 10:3, Jer 46:15, Eze 34:21).

Someone or something in honour/glow clothe or oneself exalt (Ex 23:3; Lev 19:15,32; Prov 25:6; Isa 45:2; 63:1; Lam 5:12). Hyphenated; ceremonial-adornment distinguished from H1926 hadar 'glory' (noun).
Dan-aramaic-glorify-the-Most-High-forever and Dan-aramaic-praise-and-glorify-Him and Dan-aramaic-fame-and-glorification (Dan 4:31,34; 5:23). Hyphenated.

Dan-aramaic-majesty-of-my-kingdom and Dan-aramaic-for-the-glory and Dan-aramaic-splendour-for-glory (Dan 4:27,33; 5:18). Hyphenated to distinguish majesty-splendour-aramaic-aspect from H1926 hadar 'glory'.
Proper noun Edomite king; Gen 36:39; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Hadar.
Sacred dignity of worship (1Chr 16:29; 2Chr 20:21; Ps 29:2; 96:9; Prov 14:28). Hyphenated to distinguish majesty-splendour-aspect from H1935 hod 'majesty' and H1926 hadar.
Personal pronoun 3ms. Also used as demonstrative ('that one'). English 'he' covers the pronoun; demonstrative function follows from context-position.
Aramaic pers.pron 3ms; parallel to Hebrew hu; concordantly compound with language-marker.
First-sense hava; snow falls-down on earth; Job 37:6.
Archaic-be-become in blessing-Esau and weariness-life (Gen 27:29; Eccl 2:22; 11:3). Hyphenated to distinguish be-become-exist-aspect from homonym H1933a hawah-I 'fall' and H1961 hayah.
Aramaic; concordantly identical to H1961 hayah Hebrew ('become').
Royal or divine glow, dignity; concordantly 'majesty'.
Proper noun, Asher tribe-head son of Zophah; 1Chr 7:37; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Hod.
Proper noun, Levi-clan returnees; Neh 7:43; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Hodvah.
Half-tribe-Manasseh-family-head and Benjamite and Levite-family-ancestor (1Chr 3:24; 5:24; 9:7; Ezra 2:40). English convention: Hodaviah. 'YHWH-praise'; family with H1935 hod.
Proper noun, son of Elioenai-David-branch; 1Chr 3:24; concordantly transliterated.
Judah-wife of Mered and Levite-expounders and covenant-sealers (1Chr 4:19; Neh 8:7; 9:5; 10:10,13,18). English convention: Hodiah. 'Majesty-is-YHWH'; family with H1935 hod.
A Levite who supported the explanation of the law and signed the covenant under Nehemiah - Nehemiah 8:7, 9:5, 10:10, 10:13, 10:18; name means 'my praise is YHWH'.
Pernicious longing, mischievous-desire (Proverbs, Psalms); the hyphenated English marks malicious craving.
Isa-calamity-upon-calamity-shall-come and Eze-mischief-on-mischief and Isa-doom-unforeseen (Isa 47:11; Eze 7:26). Hyphenated to distinguish calamity-ruin-doom-aspect from H7451 ra 'evil'.
Proper noun, king of Hebron; Josh 10:3; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Hoham.
Aramaic-go-move of king or fire (Ezra 5:5; 6:5; 7:13; Dan 3:25; 4:34). Hyphenated to distinguish go-walk-aspect from H236 azal-aramaic 'go-away-aramaic'; Aramaic cognate of H1980 halakh.
Hapax Eccl 10:13 mouth's-end-madness; sub-sense H1947 holeloth folly (masculine).
Tumult-unrest-stir in city or crowd (Ruth 1:19; Deut 7:23; 1Sam 4:5; 1Kgs 1:45; Ps 55:3; Mic 2:12). Hyphenated to distinguish confusion-tumult-aspect from H2000 hamam 'in-confusion-bring'.
Proper noun variant Hemam son of Lotan; 1Chr 1:39; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Homam.
Proper noun, son of Jeconiah; 1Chr 3:18; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Hoshama.
Proper noun ('deliverance'); original name of Joshua, and prophet Hosea, and last king of Israel; concordantly transliterated.
Hoshaiah-leader-people's-leader-wall-dedication and Hoshaiah-father-Azariah-Jeremiah-mocker and Hoshaiah-after-temple-procession (Neh 12:32; Jer 42:1; 43:2). English convention: Hoshaiah.

Original concordant: Hodaviah-Levitical-priest-post-exile-clan-head-temple. 1Chr-and-Hodaviah-the-son-of-Hassenuah and Ezra-the-children-of-Hodaviah-seventy-four (1Chr 9:7; Ezra 2:40 par-spelling-Hodewah). Hyphenated.
Harvest-shout at winepress or war-cry (Isa 16:9,10; Jer 25:30; 48:33; 51:14; Eze 30:5). Hyphenated to preserve joy-cry-context.
Root hyh/hwh, dynamic: become, happen. Hebrew has no verb for static being (nominal sentence carries that). 'Become' preserves the dynamic character; 'be' loses it.
Job: 'if my grief and my calamity were weighed'; Job 6:2.
Loanword from Sumerian/Akkadian; both royal palace and YHWH-temple; the hyphenated English preserves both.
Aramaic form of hekhal (H1964); royal palace Nebuchadnezzar (Dan 4:4,29), Belshazzar (Dan 5:5), YHWH-temple (Ezra 4:14, 5:14-15, 6:5, Dan 5:2-3); concordantly 'palace-temple-aramaic'.
Proper noun, son of Lotan; Gen 36:22; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Hemam.

Wise-man named alongside Solomon (1Kgs 4:31); Levitical singer and prophet, son of Joel, grandson of Samuel (1Chr 6:33, 15:17-19, 16:41-42, 25:1-6, 2Chr 5:12, 35:15); poet of Ps 88; concordantly transliterated.
Liquid measure about 3.6 litres, used at offerings; transliteration retained.

Original concordant: festival-joy-praise-harvest-feast. Lev-fourth-year-shall-all-fruit-be-holy-festival-joy-LORD and Judg-they-went-out-of-the-vineyards-and-the-grape-treading-festival-joy (Lev 19:24; Judg 9:27). Hyphenated.

Strengthened demonstrative pronoun 'that-yonder-over-there' (Gen 37:19; Judg 6:20; 1Sam 14:1; 17:26; 20:19; 2Kgs 4:25; 23:17; Eze 36:35; Dan 8:16). Hyphenated; deictic-strengthened distinct from H2088 ze.
Walking-passages or caravan-journey (Job 6:19; Nah 2:6; Hab 3:6; Ps 68:25; Prov 31:27). Hyphenated to distinguish journey-walk-aspect from H4109 mahalakh; family with H1980 halakh.
Root hlk. Iterative/habitual motion (vs. yalak, purely directional). 'Walk' covers both physical and figurative 'walk-with'.
Dan-aramaic-walking-in-midst-fire and Dan-aramaic-Nebuchadnezzar-walked-palace-Babel and Ezra-aramaic-keeping (Dan 3:25; 4:26,34; Ezra 6:5). Hyphenated.
Honey that in forest of itself flowed; 1Sam 14:26.
Original concordant: shine-glance-radiate-give-light. Job-God-moon-not-shines and Job-stars-not-pure-shine and Isa-no-more-shines-sun-on-you (Job 25:5; 29:3; 31:26; Isa 13:10). Hyphenated.
Root hll. Piel-shine, boast, praise. 'Praise' preserves the praise-utterance.

Third homonym distinguished from halal-I (shine, H1984a) and halal-II (praise, H1984b); Poel/Poal/Hithpoel: act-foolish/madly (Job 12:17 'he-makes counsellors-fools', 1Sam 21:14, Eccl 1:17, 2:2,12, 7:7, Ps 5:6, 73:3, 75:5).
With heavy blow strike; sometimes of tent-peg-driving (Judg 5:22,26; 1Sam 14:16; Ps 74:6; 141:5; Prov 23:35; Isa 16:8; 28:1; 41:7). Hyphenated; distinguishes heavy-blow-action from H5221 nakah.
Proper noun, Asher tribe-head brother of Shomer; 1Chr 7:35; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Helem.

Demonstrative-place-adverb 'unto-here/hitherward' distinguished from henna (hither, H2008) by direction-to-this-point-aspect (Ex 3:5 YHWH-to-Moses at-burning-bush, Judg 18:3, Ruth 2:14, 1Sam 14:38, 2Sam 7:18, 20:16).
Proper noun, place where Zuzim were defeated; Gen 14:5; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ham.
Personal pronoun 3mp. Counterpart of hu (H1931, 3ms). 'They' is standard plural.
Aramaic personal pronoun third person plural (Ezra 4:10,23; 5:11,12,15; 6:5; 7:17; Dan 2:34,35,44; 3:22,27). Concordantly via '-aramaic'.
Root hmh (roar). Tumultuous multitude. Semantically parallel to rov (H7230). Concordantly 'multitude' for both; Strong-distinction preserved.

Original concordant: proper-name-Hamon-Gog-multitude-of-Gog. Proper noun Hamon-Gog ('multitude of Gog') - compound place-name for valley where Gog is buried - in Ezekiel 39:11 (it shall be called the valley of the multitude of Gog) and Ezekiel 39:15.
Proper noun ('multitude-city') Gog-grave; Eze 39:16; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Hamonah.
Rumbling or tumult - in Ezekiel 1:24 (as the noise of a great army) and Jeremiah 11:16 (with the noise of a great tumult He has kindled fire on it); from H1993 hamah (roar, woel).
Qal: shatter-shock, bring into panic (God against enemies); the hyphenated English marks effect.
Proper noun; opponent in Esther; concordantly transliterated.
Aramaic-golden necklace as honour-distinction (Dan 5:7,16,29). Hyphenated to preserve Aramaic-neck-jewel-aspect; loanword from Persian.
Pers.pron. 3 pers. pl. feminine: they (Leah's children 'they came'); the hyphenated English marks gender.
Presentative particle, secondary form of hinneh (H2009). Concordantly parallel 'behold!'.

Aramaic-cognate of-Hebrew-H518a im (if) distinguished by Aramaic-language-form in-Daniel (Dan 2:5-6 Nebuchadnezzar's-threat 'if-aramaic you-do-not-make-known-to-me the-dream and-its-interpretation, you-shall-be-cut-in-pieces').
Third person plural feminine personal pronoun; distinguished from hennah I (hither); the hyphenated English marks gender.
Direction-adverb (especially with Kamatz); distinguished from henah II (they-feminine); concordantly 'hither'.
Presentative particle that draws attention. 'Behold!' preserves the deictic function; 'see' loses the attention-call.
Place-name 'Hinnom' in construct 'valley/son of Hinnom' south of Jerusalem (Josh 15:8, 18:16, 2Kgs 23:10, 2Chr 28:3, 33:6, Jer 7:31-32, 19:2-6, 32:35); concordantly transliterated.
